issue.title: [GH-28] New Plantuml pipeline for visualization

repository.name: kieker
repository.description: Kieker is an observability framework, that consists of an monitoring and tracing agent, and compatible analysis tools

issue.body:
Implementation of plantuml pipeline for diagram generation as a standalone featurebased on the current main branch of the upstream repository.

It contains
- a new plantuml pipeline for sequence diagrams generation (before it was pic)
- a new plantuml pipeline for call trees and dependency graphs (uses plantumls internal Graphviz engine now)

body:
I can reproduce it locally using the following command:
```bash
./gradlew publishMavenJavaPublicationToMavenRepository
```
Probably the current jacoco v0.8.6 cannot handle new dependencies built againt jdk21
I will try to configure the new repository address and tokens by pushing to the main branch directly.

I checked that we use the latest SNAPSHOT by configuring `pom.xml`:

```xml
<repositories>
  <repository>
      <name>Central Portal Snapshots</name>
      <id>central-portal-snapshots</id>
      <url>https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/</url>
      <releases>
          <enabled>false</enabled>
      </releases>
      <snapshots>
          <enabled>true</enabled>
      </snapshots>
  </repository>
</repositories>

<dependencies>
  <dependency>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>net.kieker-monitoring</groupId>
    <artifactId>kieker</artifactId>
    <version>2.0.3-SNAPSHOT</version>
  </dependency>
```

body:
Thanks, that looks interesting. Running `make gen-java` makes it possible to create the files without wrong ownership (the group is still root, but the user is correct). Looking at the generated code, `TracesData.parseFrom` might be able to read OpenTelemetry data. I'll have a look at it.

OpenTelemetry itself seems to have the source for serializing traces in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/tree/main/exporters/otlp/common/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/exporter/internal/otlp/traces. Unfortunately, they only have a marshaller (and no unmarshaller).

After having a further look at it, it is not necessary to compile the proto definitions on our own - including 

```
implementation 'io.opentelemetry.proto:opentelemetry-proto:1.7.0-alpha'
implementation 'com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java:3.25.1'
```

as dependencies also works.

Using a netty server, we can receive the traces with their spans and reconstruct the call trees. The branch https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/tree/GH-13-GetOERFromProto contains the current state.

There are two main issues here:
- OpenTelemetry stores the call trees using references to parent ids instead of the eoi / ess approach of Kieker. This makes it necessary to wait for the parent span to arrive, put the parent span into the Kieker trace, and then put the child span into the Kieker trace. (https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/67c9e1eca916a86b1cc6695118b117dd42efe95c/tools/otel-transformer/src/kieker/tools/oteltransformer/receiver/OtlpGrpcReceiverStage.java#L57) For this, we need to maintain a mapping from traces to the last eoi and from spans to their ess - these mappings get bigger as the program execution continues. We would need to have some way of telling when a trace is over (which we do not get from Otel, I'm afraid)
- Most of Otels calls are not method calls, but REST calls, that happen on some server. We would need to get the execution container (i.e., the container instance with IP), and the deployment component (which would usually be a class, but here, we could use anything). Otel seems to have a range of attributes (`rpc.service`, `net.peer.name`, `net.sock.peer.addr`, `peer.address` at least) that store the service / IP, the `code.namespace`, `code.function` and `service.instance.id`, which we use for the Otel->Kieker conversion seems not to be standard.

I'll have a look into this during the next days.

issue.title: [GH-8] Move to JUnit 5

repository.name: kieker
repository.description: Kieker is an observability framework, that consists of an monitoring and tracing agent, and compatible analysis tools

issue.body:
Currently, the JUnit version is mixed in Kieker, parts of it use JUnit 4, which is backed by a centralized version: https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/7e8f215f779de8274aa58f8ea73ca812a0a9b8ce/monitoring/core/build.gradle#L84 and parts of it use JUnit 5, which is backed by a individually defined dependency in every build.gradle: https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/7e8f215f779de8274aa58f8ea73ca812a0a9b8ce/tools/delta/build.gradle#L39

This leads to dependabot PRs, that only update parts of the dependencies, e.g., https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/pull/2881

This is not very nice. We should
- [ ] Introduce a managed version for JUnit 5, so all tools use the same JUnit Jupiter dependency
- [ ] Update everything to JUnit 5

Probably, the first thing is easier and should be done immediately, the second thing takes a bit of effort.

issue.title: Kieker slf4j does not work in MooBench

repository.name: moobench
repository.description: Micro-benchmarks for quantification of the performance overhead caused by observability frameworks

issue.body:
Currentl, slf4j does not work in MooBench:

SLF4J(W): No SLF4J providers were found.
SLF4J(W): Defaulting to no-operation (NOP) logger implementation
SLF4J(W): See https://www.slf4j.org/codes.html#noProviders for further details.

We could add for example logback (`implementation 'ch.qos.logback:logback-classic:1.5.6`) into the benchmark, but this would kind of be an unfair comparison, since other benchmarking tools (such as OpenTelemetry) would require to have a library on the classpath that they don't use. However, without this, debugging Kieker is cumbersome, so probably we'll need to add some logging backend directly to the Kieker-java variant (and all other variants requiring a logging backend).

Instructions for ActiveMQ

Download

Download Apache ActiveMQ: http://activemq.apache.org/activemq-550-release.html

  • There are two different distributions, one for Unix/Linux/Cygwin and another one for Windows

Preparing the Example

Copy the following Jar files from the ActiveMQ distribution to the example's lib directory

  • activemq-all-5.5.0.jar (to be found in the base directory)
  • slf4j-log4j12-1.5.11.jar (to be found in lib/optional)
  • log4j-1.2.14.jar (to be found in lib/optional)
kieker.monitoring.writer.jms.AsyncJMSWriter.ProviderUrl=tcp://127.0.0.1:61616/

kieker.monitoring.writer.jms.AsyncJMSWriter.ContextFactoryType=org.apache.activemq.jndi.ActiveMQInitialContextFactory

Preparing and starting the ActiveMQ Server

Unix/Linux/Cygwin

chmod +x bin/activemq

$ bin/activemq setup ~/.activemqrc
INFO: Creating configuration file: /home/avanhoorn/.activemqrc
INFO: It's recommend to limit access to '/home/avanhoorn/.activemqrc' to the priviledged user
INFO: (recommended: chown avanhoorn:nogroup '/home/avanhoorn/.activemqrc'; chmod 600 '/home/avanhoorn/.activemqrc')

In case you get the following error

$ bin/activemq 
/bin/sh: Can't open

you need to convert the the windows line-breaks to Unix line-breaks, e.g. using your favorite editor or the dos2unix tool.

Adjust the file owner and permissions

$ chmod 600 '/home/avanhoorn/.activemqrc'

Run

$ bin/activemq start
INFO: Loading '/home/avanhoorn/.activemqrc'
INFO: Using java '/usr/bin/java'
INFO: Starting - inspect logfiles specified in logging.properties and log4j.properties to get details
INFO: pidfile created : '/home/avanhoorn/svn_work/kieker/software/kieker/trunk/examples/userguide/appendix-JMS/apache-activemq-5.5.0/data/activemq.pid' (pid '4540')

Stop

bin/activemq stop

HornetQ configuration

Add the following queue to the config/stand-alone/non-clustered/hornetq-jms.xml configuration file:

Run

Note, that the run.sh most be called from within the bin/ directory!

$ ./run.sh

author André van Hoorn -- Thu, 24 Nov 2011 14:34:03 +0100

I agree, that we should think about tweaking this concept in a later step --- e.g. adding, as alternatives, your proposed solution or the support of using Java annotations (as detailed below).

In general I think that our current implementation supports these extensions in later steps.

Replying to KIEKER-1047 Done :
> Better would be an automatic delegation of each incoming call on a port to a method like:
> void newEvent(IInputPort inPort, Object event)
> This method would be enforced by the AbstractAnalysisPlugin and a concrete default implementation of the AbstractInputPort could provide the delegation.

This would result in a switch/case block or if-then-else cascade in the newEvent method, right?

Could be implemented by special input ports (e.g.) created by a factory in the super class. These input ports transparently redirect the incoming event to the common handler function of the plugin.

> A remaining problem is, when to tell the OutputPort where to deliver its messages. You must not let this escape during the construction of the Plugin.

I don't see the problem here. The plugin (implementation) knows best when to deliver records to the right output port(s).

> Another approach might be the move of the construction of ports into the Abstract Super class (in registerInputPort). Thus this class is simply called several times with the names (or whatever) of the wanted ports and then correctly creates them.

Some time ago, we thought about using Java annotations for this purpose. These would be used to mark and configure input ports, e.g.:

InputPort(name="myInputPort", types={MonitoringRecord.class})
public void newEvent(Object event) {

}

In a later step, we might support this as an alternative way of declaring input ports. What do you think?

author nils-christian -- Fri, 15 Aug 2014 14:06:09 +0200

I added a possible solution in a branch with ca20ec477a2006f2d9307ee1622ea18d98d2debc.

The solution allows to configure a limit for the cache:

## The maximal size of the signature cache. This is a weak limit, as the cache can exceed this size
## slightly in practical application.
## Set to 0 for an unbounded cache.
kieker.monitoring.adaptiveMonitoring.maxCacheSize=0
#
## The behaviour of the signature cache, if the maximal size is bounded.
## 0: The cache ignores entries once the maximal size is reached.
## 1: The cache removes a (semi)random entry from the cache once the maximal size is exceeded.
kieker.monitoring.adaptiveMonitoring.boundedCacheBehaviour=0

The limit is weak, as a stronger limit would require additional synchronization in the map. The cache allows two behaviours, shown in the above listing.

A perfomant and thread-safe LRU cache would require some more work, I guess.

Opinions on this before I merge it back into the master?

author nils-christian -- Mon, 27 Oct 2014 14:20:41 +0100

A connector is available since adbb2c983d7aeace7f4f793e27e6d9d978a7135b. The connector can be configured for a specific context, port, and URL. If, for instance, the connector is configured to use port 8080, context / and URL /kieker/rest/monitoringRecord, one can use the URL http://localhost:8080/kieker/rest/monitoringRecord to send new records. The connector expects records to be sent in JSON format as a POST request. The JSON object should contain three fields class, timestamp, and values. The values field should be an array containing the values to deserialize the record. Each field should contain only strings.

An exemplaric JSON string:

{
  "class": "kieker.common.record.jvm.UptimeRecord",
  "timestamp": "1412872210980520945",
  "values": ["1412872210980520945", "SE-host", "VM", "20000"]
}

When I tried to let a record (ExtendedStorableDetectionResult) inherit from an existing one (StorableDetectionResult), I ran into a test failure in TestRecordSerialization which stated, that I had passed too many objects to the constructor.

The cause for this was, that the constructor passes the object array (containing all parameters as Object) to the parent class constructor which checks (AbstractMonitoringRecord.checkArray(..)) the number of items in the array with its own number of required parameters. This obviously leads to a problem, as I added another attribute in the inheriting class.

Compared with another inheriting record class (CompilationRecord inheriting from AbstractJVMRecord) the check in the superclass is not done in AbstractJVMRecord but is not done in the StorableDetectionResult. This leads to the failing when testing in the ExtendedStorableDetectionResult.
For now I implemented a workaround for this failing test (passing a subset of the object array), but it might be better if there would be one way to do it consistently (either with or without the check in the superclass).

author Fabian Keller -- Mon, 25 Nov 2013 23:09:22 +0100

Web automation testing can be easily achieved by writing tests using a syntax related to Gherkin's syntax. Thus tests are easy to read, to understand and to write. In order to translate the test language into executable code, we need a framework like jBehave, which maps the step definitions to methods in order to have an executable version of the tests.

A combination of jBehave and Selenium Webdriver can be used to automate web regression testing. There is a github repository demonstrating how to setup the two tools to work together.

To automatically run the tests in the cloud SauceLabs provides a free plan for open source projects like TravisCI for Continous Integration, which can also run the tests on mobile devices and all major browsers.

Personally, I use these tests to automatically do functional regression testing of websites and web applications developed in PHP. For PHP there is a handy framework which already supplies a lot of the step definitions commonly needed. The following list is an excerpt of the frameworks' definitions to underline how powerful the tools work together:

Given I am on the homepage
    - Opens homepage.

Given I am on "page"
    - Opens specified page.
    
 When I move backward one page
    - Moves backward one page in history.
    
 When I press "button"
    - Presses button with specified id|name|title|alt|value.
    
 When I follow "link"
    - Clicks link with specified id|title|alt|text.
    
 When I fill in "field" with "value"
    - Fills in form field with specified id|name|label|value.
 
 When I select "option" from "select"
    - Selects option in select field with specified id|name|label|value.
    
 When I additionally select "option" from "select"
    - Selects additional option in select field with specified id|name|label|value.
    
 When I check "option"
    - Checks checkbox with specified id|name|label|value.
  
 When I attach the file "..." to "field"
    - Attaches file to field with specified id|name|label|value.
    
 Then I should be on "page"
    - Checks, that current page PATH is equal to specified.
    
 Then the url should match pattern "..."
    - Checks, that current page PATH matches regular expression.

An example of a real test case that tests the search function of Wikipedia:

Feature: Search
  In order to see a word definition
  As a website user
  I need to be able to search for a word

  Scenario: Searching for a page that does exist
    Given I am on "/wiki/Main_Page"
    When I fill in "search" with "Behavior Driven Development"
    And I press "searchButton"
    Then I should see "agile software development"

  Scenario: Searching for a page that does NOT exist
    Given I am on "/wiki/Main_Page"
    When I fill in "search" with "Glory Driven Development"
    And I press "searchButton"
    Then I should see "Search results"

This ticket refers to the desired ability of changing filter configurations at runtime. Concrete example: change forecasting algorithm in OPAD depending on current workload characteristics.

A possible approach could be to
1. Add a boolean attribute like updateable to the Property annotation for configuration variables that marks variables as being (not) updateable (default: false)
1. interface method like updateConfiguration (Configuration config) to be implemented by filters. Updateable fields are reinitialized in this method.

Some reusable support could be provided by the abstract super class (e.g. ensuring that only updateable field are read).

As discussed yesterday:

1. Extension of the Property annotation by a boolean updateable field make sense
1. The abstract super class can provide a convenience function to access this property (boolean isPropertyUpdateable(String))
1. We are in favour of not keeping a local copy of Configuration objects in filters. Hence, configuration properties are held in local variables.
1. Instead, updateConfiguration (Configuration config) makes sense. Pattern to update could be à la if(isPropertyUpdateable(..) { /* update field */ })
1. In addition to the changes of the filter classes, methods are needed to lookup filters, e.g., using unique IDs. However, steps 1-4 are independent of this.

About the constants: Java provides the size via Integer.SIZE, Double.SIZE, etc. There are only two problems: Strings and Booleans. As Strings are handled via a registry, they have the size of an int. Booleans, however, have a size depending on the actual JVM and do not provide a size field.

I agree with André that we should use these available constants for the calculation of the size. The JUnit test makes sure that we don't disimprove the code.

author rju -- Thu, 24 Sep 2015 14:40:47 +0200

Thanks to the gradle build scripts, we can divide Kieker in different packages or modules. As discussed before, this might be helpful to address special use cases and issues users have. For example, a professional user wants to use Kieker for instrumentation. Presently, we provide one Kieker package including everything. In this package we provide

  • tooling in bin
  • three different kieker libraries build/libs to be used with a software system which contain monitoring and analysis stuff all together.
  • documentation
  • examples
  • Java documentation
  • And a large list of libraries which might be required in different configurations of Kieker

From a user's perspective this is suboptimal. It is motivated by the idea: Download one blob and you get everything. This is a good idea if you want to try Kieker for the first time, like students or for evaluation. However, it is a bad idea when you want to use it in production or research.

It would be better to have:

  • kieker-monitoring package including kieker-common and kieker-monitoring without additional stuff and a README containing information on the libraries required to be able to run it in different contexts.
  • A library package containing all these libraries.
  • kieker-analysis as library
  • kieker-tools

It might me useful to make separate downloads for the Kieker online/runtime analysis tools (admin, runtime) and Kieker analysis tools (developer/engineer, design time).

author nils-christian -- Sat, 31 May 2014 16:15:10 +0200

Suggestion for the whole build process of the live demo:


- kieker/examples/JavaEEServletContainerExample
- jetty


- ...


- jPetStore


- ...


- ant.xml


- livedemo


- ...


- ant.xml


- ant.xml

Basically the ant files in jPetStore and livedemo compile and pack the corresponding web applications. The ant file in the base directory calls the ant scripts from jPetStore and livedemo. It copies the packed war files into Jetty's webapps directory and unpacks them there. This way we can provide the applications as war files (and see if we can deploy them into the Tomcat) and can still have the jPetStore in folders.

Usually I would prefer Maven for this whole task, but I wouldn't recommend to mix Maven and Ant scripts for Kieker and its examples.

That is the reason why we support sld4j.

The main reason for providing our own implementation is rooted in the monitoring side of Kieker:

We usually try to employ the logging also used by our System under Monitoring (SUM). However, in some cases, this is not practicable, e.g., if you also want to instrument the logging of the system. Thus, an own implementation that can be configured independently is mandatory.

Furthermore, in small setups the use of SLF4j might be "overkill". Simple calls to jdk logging are more than sufficient.

In summary: I see no reason for such a switch. If you have any actual arguments besides: others do it too! feel free to comment.

RServe within R does return the exit code and it could be propagated via q(status=RServe()). However, using "R CMD Rserve", this is not possible.

Possible fix for the script (now checks whether process returning + whether pkill successful):

case "$1" in
    start)
	echo -n "Trying to start Rserve..."
	R CMD Rserve --vanilla &
	#R CMD Rserve.dbg --vanilla > /tmp/rserve.dbg.log &
	RET=$?
	if [ $RET = 0 ] && (ps ax | grep -i "rserve --no-save" | grep -qv grep); then
		echo "done."
	else
		echo "failed (exit status >0 or Rserve could not be started)."
	fi
	exit 1
        ;;
    stop)
	echo -n "Trying to stop Rserve..."
	if pkill Rserve; then
	    echo "done."
	else 
	    echo "failed"
	    exit 1
	fi
        ;;
    *)
        ## If no parameters are given, print which are available.
        echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop}"
        exit 0
        ;;
esac

author rju -- Sun, 14 Sep 2014 13:52:05 +0200

In testing practice performing integration, performance and other scenario based tests is a totally different task to component tests along well-defined borders. Unit-tests should only focus on in language interfaces. IO can be tested also, but a couple of requirements must be fulfilled:

  1. Testing file creation, all files of a test should be located in one common directory for the test, which must be disjunct from all other tests.
  2. Other IO tests must also acquire disjunct resources. For TCP, UDP communication, this can be done by allocating different ports for each test. However, there is no system service where you can fetch a free port number for your test. Probing for free ports can be implemented. However, as probing and allocating cannot be performed in one system operation, race conditions may occur. A better solution would the execution of those tests in a virtual machine.

As we do not realize our own IP protocol, we do not need to unit-test that protocol stack level. We can, therefore, test the data before it is send.

For integration tests we could indeed use one or more virtual machines which get their IP address automatically on startup. Such infrastructure could be realized with virtual box or KVM and does not need OpenStack. It might be a good idea to let a bachelor student write his/her thesis on this topic.

In short: I agree with Nils to separate the classical unit tests from the integration tests. As a first step we should separate the tests to an appropriate package without changing its underlying technology.

It is available at the release site. However, the compiler in Kieker itself does not support it.
I am not happy with the CLI compiler, as it has several short comings. First, it requires an extensive set of parameters. Second, it relies on Eclipse plugins, but is not a real headless RCP application. Therefore, the JDT scanner does not work, which is the cause for this special Kieker compiler version.

We have to rethink this compiler, either as RCP application or use the new headless features of Xtext (which have been announced). In the latter case the JDT scanner has to go, which would not allow to use IRL files to extend existing Kieker record types. Maybe it is possible to add the IRL files to the JAR and then do not require a JDT scanner after all. But would that work in a CLI compiler version? I don't know.

The feature itself is present and available through the update site.

The language supports transient properties.

author rju -- Thu, 11 Jan 2018 19:32:20 +0100

The language and generator supports transient properties. However, the current code generation works as follows:

  • The transient property is created without final, as it is not set in all constructors.
  • The parameter constructor sets the property by parameter
  • The array constructor sets the property from an array value
  • The deserializer constructor sets the property to a default values

Replying to KIEKER-1412 Done (comment 3) holger.knoche:
> I'm not sure if requiring Java 7 (which is already past the end of public updates) for building Kieker is really a big issue. Of course, we should ensure that Kieker still runs under Java 6 as this version is still widely used in productive environments.

In the past, we've had bad experience with building with Java version N with a configured target version <N. While the byte code may be compatible with <N, it does not prevent you from using JDK library functions not available in <N. But may be find a good "hybrid" solution for that.

author Thomas F. Düllmann -- Fri, 30 Sep 2016 17:19:42 +0200

As even Java 7 is comparably old by now, we should think about whether it might be better to directly go up to Java 8.

OK, but this means that our plan to generate a 1.6-compliant java agent will not work.

author Unknown -- Thu, 8 Dec 2016 17:36:52 +0100

Right. Perhaps it's time to stop the support for Java 6. Or I use the old API for the writers. It's not much effort to change the implementation parts. But how much longer should we support Java 6?

One idea we had in mind was to switch to Java 7 and additionally generate a monitoring agent also compiled with Java 6. Without the use of NIO.2 I expect this to be easy. Do you have numbers on the performance impact on the writers regarding the (not) use of NIO.2?

author Unknown -- Thu, 8 Dec 2016 18:00:35 +0100

No, I haven't. I mainly used the NIO.2 API because it requires fewer lines of code.

Two reasons:

  • The example depends on the jar-file and not simply on one or more of the subprojects.
  • Building the jar-file depends on all checks and tests.

Possible solutions:

  • Let the example depend on the Kieker-Maven-Dependency
  • Let the example depend (during development) on one or more of the subprojects
  • Do not execute the checks and tests for the jar-file

See instructions in Gradle (2.2.1) User Guide Chapter 62 "The Gradle Wrapper"

"The Gradle Wrapper (henceforth referred to as the “wrapper”) is the preferred way of starting a Gradle build.
The wrapper is a batch script on Windows, and a shell script for other operating systems. When you start a
Gradle build via the wrapper, Gradle will be automatically downloaded and used to run the build.

The wrapper is something you check into version control. By distributing the wrapper should with your project,
anyone can work with it without needing to install Gradle beforehand. Even better, users of the build are
guaranteed to use the version of Gradle that the build was designed to work with. Of course, this is also great for
continuous integration servers (i.e. servers that regularly build your project) as it requires no configuration on
the server."

Implemented the following changes in changeset:ff782cbec292cd38b8a84763530608122bbdf391/kieker-git

Added the wrapper script by
1. Adding the following task to our build.gradle file:
{{

{ task wrapper(type: Wrapper) \{ gradleVersion = '2.2.1' }

}}}
2. Executing the task:
{{

{ avhAndrè van Hoorn-ThinkPad-RSS:0:~/git_work/kieker <1533-gradle>* $ gradle wrapper }

}}
3. Adding the downloaded files to the Git:
{{

{ avhAndrè van Hoorn-ThinkPad-RSS:0:~/git_work/kieker <1533-gradle>* $ git add gradlew gradlew.bat }

}}

The script can now be used by calling ./gradlew(.bat) and the usual Gradle options. On the first call of the script, the specified Gradle version is downloaded in installed (under *NIX into the /home/avh/.gradle/wrapper/dists/ directory).

author nils-christian -- Wed, 28 Jan 2015 21:27:01 +0100

Usually Gradle projects are build in an incremental way. However, the build of our monitoring part leads to an interesting issue. We are using the AspectJ post compiler (iajc) to weave some additional code into the class files of our AspectJ probes. The iajc task runs after the usual compile tasks. That means, that we change the output (the class files) of the usual compile process. Why is this problem? Because Gradle saves snapshots from the input and output files of each task and uses them to check whether a task is up to date or not (this is detailed in Section 15.9.2 of the Gradle documentation). Modifying the output of the compile tasks lets Gradle assume that the compile task is not up to date. I check whether there is some kind of a workaround or a solution.

userhost:0:~/git-repos/kieker.git>git fetch
userhost:0:~/git-repos/kieker.git>git push --mirror

Push script:

userhost:0:~>cat git-push-mirror-kieker.sh
#!/bin/bash

cd ~/git-repos/kieker.git
git fetch 
git push --mirror

Add script to crontab (using crontab -e), configuring push every 15 minutes:

*/15   *       *     *     *  /home/user/git-push-mirror-kieker.sh > /dev/null 2>&1

    I do not understand why the method parameter type is not just CPUUtilizationRecord if you cast anyway. This present implementation has two issues:

    3. Super call

In

{https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/6277a4dc70fbeea83c111e75c95ba851d1e56ffc/subprojects/code-quality/src/main/groovy/org/gradle/api/plugins/quality/internal/findbugs/FindBugsClasspathValidator.java|FindBugsClasspathValidator}

the findbugs plugin checks the type of the found findbugs versions. The used findbugs version is determined in getFindbugsVersion which uses the first findbugs library matching "findbugs-(.*)
.jar". In our case this is 2.0.3 (after I added the -$VERSION) the the jar files.

However, the setup also works, when Java 8 is installed and the gradle script is executed with Java 8. In that case it should switch to findbugs 3.0.1, but the code does not support this conclusion.

Re Source/target language used by the Java compiler: this is dangerous! It does lead to the right bytecode version but does not use/consider the source/target runtime libraries. author Thomas F. Düllmann -- Tue, 2 Feb 2016 13:16:44 +0100

The problem and solution are only partly related to Kieker. I integrated Kieker as a seperate OSGI bundle in my programm (PMX). This resulted in different classloaders for my programm (PMX) and Kieker. Therefore, simple coppying of new record types to PMX did not add it to Kieker trace parsing. The solution was to create a fragment project which uses the same Java classloader applied for the Kieker bundle. For more details see: https://se3.informatik.uni-wuerzburg.de/descartes/pmx/commits/cocome

author SoerenHenning -- Mon, 28 Nov 2016 17:48:21 +0100

First and (maybe) most important question is: Has EList really lookup of O(n)? EList has a contains() method (as well as its super class List), but this method has a more complex implementation. See source code.

author SoerenHenning -- Thu, 1 Dec 2016 18:08:02 +0100

contains() has normaly O(n), but EMF uses some hacks to make it faster. For example, if there exists a reverse reference. However, even if contains() would be fast enough, we would still have the problem that we first have to generate a child before we can check whether it exists already in its parent. That's why we need a method to look up for or get a child by its name.

author SoerenHenning -- Fri, 16 Dec 2016 10:13:23 +0100

At first, we decided to implement the third option. An implementation of this indexed entities can be found in commit d3d033d7139db26e7faac13b6ececb8294663341.

In the Kieker developers Meeting at 14 December 2016 we discussed some disadvantage of this approach. These are, for instance, an ugly casting when going from an indexed parent to an indexed child. Serializing indexed model works perfectly, however deserializing produces only object of the not indexed super type. To create an indexed sub type a deep clone would be necessary, which would be very ugly.

Therefore, we are now following the approach of Reiner, which is to model the maps directly in the EMF meta model. EMF automatically transforms this modeled maps to references. A partial implementation can be found in commit c8a23f287d3fd656006803b306c7e295fc4343f8.

author SoerenHenning -- Thu, 19 Jan 2017 14:00:49 +0100

The implementation of the "Map"-approach was considered to be suitable for our needs. Generated code of the current version of the meta model can be found in commit b2873ba4e0034ccfb884970247b63b9d88f4fddd.

However, further adjustments of the meta model will be discussed in at Kieker Developer Meeting on January 25th 2017. The corresponding issue for the new metamodel is KIEKER-1476 Open .

author rju -- Wed, 4 Oct 2017 16:28:08 +0200

In iObserve, we had a similar problem, as not all libraries are available via Maven or only using the wrong Java version. Therefore, we created our own iobserve-repository as a github project containing all libraries. The iobserve-repository https://github.com/research-iobserve/iobserve-repository includes a script to build the repository based on an eclipse installation (which would be replaced by a folder containing the libraries) and an mavenized repository folder. Therefore, it can be included in gradle or maven like this:

repositories {
     maven {url project.properties['api.baseline']}
}

Advantages of this approach:

  1. Allows to move gradually from our special sources to external sources for libraries (one library at a time, without any issues)
  2. Allows to move back to the special repository in case a proper external source becomes unavailable or provides a library only for incompatible Java version.
  3. All dependencies are outside of the Kieker repository and can use the gradle dependency mechanism
  4. Allows to use gradle bundling features
  5. Allows to improve gradle build script structure

author rju -- Wed, 8 Nov 2017 10:08:18 +0100

This example from iObserve shows two features we use to build bundles.

  • We apply the application plugin to create the bundle
  • We define how this should be represented in a maven repository (optional)

The application plugin needs only the mainClassName set, as it inherits dependencies from the parent project. However, you can still add specific dependencies from within the projects (in that case package analysis) and an external dependency (in that case jcommander).

apply plugin: 'application'

mainClassName='org.iobserve.replayer.ReplayerMain'

dependencies {
	compile project(":analysis")
	compile "com.beust:jcommander:1.60"
}

install {
    repositories.mavenInstaller {
        pom.version = version
        pom.groupId = 'org.iobserve'
        pom.artifactId = 'replayer'
    }
}

In contrast the Kieker tools uses a lot fo "resolveLibrary" features and is not able to produce bundles. It also includes tasks which should be defined in a central place (record regeneration), as this has nothing to do with creating tools.

author rju -- Wed, 14 Feb 2018 16:56:44 +0100

Performed cleanup of old `AsciiFileWriter` and `BinaryFileWriter`. And build upon their general idea a new configurable `FileWriter`.

The new `FileWriter` can use different map file, log stream, and file pool handlers.

  • `IFilePoolHandler` generates the log folder and log file names necessary for logging. Depending on the implementation it can also delete older log files depending on the implementation. Default is RotationFilePoolHandler which starts deleting files when the maximum number of files is reached.
  • `IMapFileHandler` handles map files and in general supports map file compression. Default is `TextMapFileHandler` which write the standard Kieker map files and does not support compression.
  • `AbstractLogStreamHandler` handles the log stream and an optional compression of the log stream. Default is `TextLogStreamHandler`.

The overall architecture of the `FileWriter` can be found in the attached document (if this is possible.)

author SoerenHenning -- Fri, 15 Mar 2019 13:17:43 +0100

The use case is as follows:

1. I'm writing Kieker records to a (Cassandra) database. In the database there is a table for the corresponding record type. Writing to this table is done by creating a new row (for this record) and mapping each property of this record to a field in the newly created row. This works well using the existing APIs.

2. When reading records from a table, I only define the corresponding record type (via a factory) and table rows are "deserialized" to Kieker records. However, this requires to access the individual table fields by their name. That is to say, when deserializing record from the database, I need a list of all property names of a record type – even without having an actual instance of this record type present. The concrete use case can be found here where the field columnNames needs to be set. My current workaround is to generate a "dummy" instance new MyRecord("", 0, 0).getValueNames() which is rather ugly.

Even though I highlighted the use case for Cassandra, it is likely that this issue applies to all other kinds of serialization, where records are serialized into a key-value/map-like structure (e.g., JSON) instead of a sequence of only the record's values.

Apart from that, as the constants (which can be somehow seen as record metadata) SIZE and TYPES are public, for me it seems quite inconsistent that PROPERTY_NAMES is not public.

An additional suggestion is to provide methods for returning these constants from the record factory classes. This way, everything that is required to create records in an arbitrary generic way is encapsulated in an IRecordFactory.

Since your jar is not able to instrument final fields, I tried to build it on my own and to understand the AspectJ problem. In general, Around advices on constructors setting final values do not work in Java 11 (or maybe 9+): https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64611859/is-it-possible-to-exclude-field-sets-in-aspectj/ (mwe https://github.com/DaGeRe/aspect-final-example ). As pointed out in the Stackoverflow answer, this is a general issue in AspectJ.

From my current point of view, there are two ways to fix this:

  1. Exclude Constructors from monitoring in general. This quick hack can be implemented quickly (e.g. https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/tree/java11_2 ) by change just the monitoredOperation pointcuts to Pointcut("execution(* (..))") instead of Pointcut("execution( *(..)) || execution(new(..))"). Then, constructors are also excluded from monitoring in Java 8, which is not very nice, but at least Monitoring is working in Java 11.
  2. Refactor the monitoring to use Before and After instead of Around, at least for constructors. Therefore, it would be necessary to know the signature, start time etc. in the After method, and saving them could be expensive.

Do you see another way of fixing/quick hacking this issue?

author rju -- Tue, 3 Nov 2020 13:56:53 +0100

Please note that all examples still appear in the distribution, but they are unchecked.

A key issue with our examples is that they should be build after jars have been compiled and put in a local repository for gradle or maven to find. Then subsequently, each example should be build without copy tricks. This is even more an issue when we use third party libraries which we have then to provide in our distribution instead of fetching them from their respective repository.

Current model:

  • special libs which we have to update by hand and sync with automatically updated libraries in the normal part of Kieker.
  • libraries are copied based on regex into lib folders.
  • Example is test compiled.
  • Example is test executed.
  • Example is cleaned.
  • Example is packed into the result bundles of Kieker.

Issues with that approach:

  • We have to add jars to a lib folder in our git repository which are not necessary to be there when we would use normal dependency resolving mechanisms.
  • Users of the examples have to copy files when they get our bundle and want to try it out instead of resolving it via maven/gradle
  • The copy and clean mechanism is complex comprises 92 tasks all doing something similar, but using different configurations and setups.

author DaGeRe -- Mon, 26 Jun 2023 15:36:59 +0200

After a deeper look on this, the problem is, that the DirectoryScannerStage reads all folders sequentially, and for each directory, the DirectoryReaderStage reads the folder data: https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/master/kieker-tools/src/kieker/tools/source/LogsReaderCompositeStage.java#L88

The old reader starts a bunch of threads: https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/a76e5093f86ee18f1c0365343b001296ec33e942/kieker-analysis/src/kieker/analysis/plugin/reader/filesystem/FSReader.java#L129 That add the data to a PriorityQueue:https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/a76e5093f86ee18f1c0365343b001296ec33e942/kieker-analysis/src/kieker/analysis/plugin/reader/filesystem/FSReader.java#L162C24-L162C24

To overcome the problems, it would be necessary to start separate threads again and add the data to a PriorityQueue. I do not know how to do this using the current architecture, because the DirectoryScannerStage is a AbstractProducerStage<File> which is claimed to create one entry per call.

The only option I see would be:

  • Start the {{Thread}}s inside the stage
  • Let them write into a PriorityQueue
  • Read from the queue, and send the results to the outputPort

This seems to break the original pipe and filter architecture, and has one bigger component that organizes everything internally. Is there a solution that fits better to the pipe and filter architecture, or should I implement it this way?

author rju -- Mon, 26 Jun 2023 18:15:36 +0200

To fix the time issue, we could create a TimeSequenceCorrectionStage. It would receive events and put them in an ordered list, ordered by time. After a given threshold delay, it would remove the oldest events first. On that basis, the events would be mostly sorted. And in most cases this should remove all out of time sequence issues. To do this for all events of a log, it would be quite complicated, as most logs do not fit in memory. So you have to sort chunks and then check whether they have some time overlap and merge them.

author DaGeRe -- Tue, 27 Jun 2023 18:10:58 +0200

Thanks for the idea, I’ve created an implementation: https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/commit/6c3b4dd4c61957621eefdde994340fc76a74d882

Unfortunately, that will not work in a larger scale, since if you have 5 microservices and each of this microservices is running for 10 minutes, it will have records with timestamps just distributed over these 10 minutes (each one has something at the end, each one has something in the beginning).

Therefore, we’ll need something that does this sorting, directly as part of the LogsReaderCompositeStage.

Therefore, I think the following changes are necessary:

  • The DirectoryScannerStage maintains a PriorityQueue, sorting the files by date (therefore, files with similiar timestamps would be read after each other, instead of files in one folder - a valid sorting by name would be even better, but we can add this in the future)
  • The DirecoryReaderStage redirects all output to a SorterStage

I’ll try to implement this tomorrow.

author Marius Löwe -- Fri, 21 Dec 2012 02:16:24 +0100

Recording

camstudio is easy to use for recording. You can select a different mouse pointer, highlight the mouse pointer and highlight mouse clicks. The latter doesn't work always.

You probably want to install a better codec, so the recorded files won't get too big. I used Xvid. For some reason it didn't worked to select one screen (instead of all) with this codec. But recording a fixed area matching exactly the screen works.

Also you should reduce your screen resolution before starting recording (or increase fonts etc.) to keep the video readable on lower resolutions.

Editing

Wink

Wink is nearly perfect. It combines recording and editing. It also has a mode to take screen shots (on mouse click) and reconstruct the mouse movement afterwards, which makes editing easier. Sadly it cannot output normal video files

Avidemux

Avidemux crashes often (on my computer)

Lightworks

Lightworks seems like total overkill. It is also too complicated to just start using it.

Windows Movie Maker

Windows Movie Maker is easy to use. But it has some limitations:

  • It can only output 4:3 or 16:9 aspect ratio. In other cases it adds black bars.
  • If you have Xvid install (e.g. for camstudio) you have to uninstall it. Otherwise Movie Maker cannot handle Xvid videos correctly (at least on my system).
  • It can only add text (no graphics) as overlay.

  • Modeling is quite straight forward based on the existing Java-based meta-model {br}

    (note that is includes call trees, dependency graphs, sequence diagrams etc.)

  • We know it satisfies our (current) requirements
  • Additional requirements can be implemented into the meta-model
  • Cons:
  • "Yet another (component) meta-model or ADL"
  • Interoperability with other tools/meta-models requires M2M transformations
    1. UML 2
  • Pros:
  • Existing Ecore model
  • Established, widely known/used
  • Allows modeling of static and dynamic views
  • Possible interoperability with other tools (extractors, modeling, visualization)
  • Cons:
  • Large specification (but: don't need to use all concepts)
    1. Knowledge Discovery Metamodel (KDM)
  • Pros:
  • Existing Ecore model
  • Cons:
  • Not widely known
  • Focuses on static views (as far as I know)
  • Some but not so much tool support
    1. ...

  • Modeling concepts
  • ...

author André van Hoorn -- Fri, 2 Sep 2011 20:10:57 +0200

Added a terminate() method to the AnalysisController:

    /**
     * Initiates a termination of the analysis. 
     */
    public void terminate() {
    	/* terminate the reader. After the reader has terminated, the run method()
    	 * will terminate all plugins */
    	AnalysisController.log.info("Explicit termination of the analysis. Terminating the reader ...");
    	this.logReader.terminate();
    }

Therefore, the IMonitoringReader interface has been extended by the following method:

    /**
     * Initiates a termination of the reader. This method is only used by the 
     * framework and should not be called manually to register a receiver. Use 
     * the method {link AnalysisController#terminate()} instead.
     * 
     * After receiving this notification, 
     * the reader should terminate its {link #read()} method. 
     */
    public void terminate();

The new class AnalysisControllerThread (extending the Thread class) takes an initialized AnalysisController as input and starts it in its start() method. The asynchronously running instance can be terminated by calling the AnalysisControllerThread's terminate method().

Now, the initialization and the asynchronous start of an AnalysisController looks like this:

final IMonitoringReader reader = ...
final IMonitoringRecordConsumerPlugin receiver = ...

final AnalysisController analysis = new AnalysisController();
analysis.setReader(reader);
analysis.registerPlugin(receiver);
final AnalysisControllerThread analysisThread = new AnalysisControllerThread(analysis);
analysisThread.start();

... // do some work

analysisThread.terminate();

author André van Hoorn -- Sat, 3 Sep 2011 11:25:46 +0200

Before Kieker 1.3, the data was flushed to the .dat files after each record. Unfortunately, in Kieker 1.3 we changed this behavior: we removed the explicit flush. Thus, your monitoring data would have
looked the same if you had shut down your application server.

In the meantime, we realized that this was not an intended/intuitive default behavior and changed this back. The new default behavior (i.e., from Kieker 1.4 on) is the old behavior with explicit flush after each record. This can be disabled using a new configuration parameter.

So for you, there are mainly two options:

1. Shut down the application server before analyzing the data
OR
2. (recommended) Download a nightly build from Kieker 1.4's trunk:

{br}
https://se.informatik.uni-kiel.de/kieker/download/ {br}

(But keep in mind, that this is a nightly build.)

To summarize: The issue has been resolved in the meantime (applying to Kieker 1.4).

author nils-christian -- Thu, 2 Aug 2012 18:27:13 +0200

This could be done via the java-provided MessageDigest. The problem is that the modern functions use hashes with sizes 128 or 256 Bit while the hashCode()-method within Java delivers only an Integer of 32 Bit size. If one would do it without the hashCode()- and the equals(...)-method, this could be easily implemented.

The only hash algorithms which have to be supported by every java-platform are the following:

  • MD5 (128 Bit)
  • SHA-1 (160 Bit)
  • SHA-256 (256 Bit)
    This means also that there is no (by the java-platform guaranteed) algorithm we could use which would result in 32 Bit hashes.

author André van Hoorn -- Tue, 13 Sep 2011 11:16:05 +0200

Yes, the full range (including negative values) is used. Only -1 must NOT be returned by getUniqueTraceId(), as -1 is used as a marker for "not yet assigned"/"invalid" in OperationExecutionRecords.

Having thought about the implementation again, I concluded that it does implement the desired behavior also in multi-threaded scenarios.

My concern was a concurrent execution like the following one, but it seems to fine:

(this.lastThreadId = -2)
Thread A: id = -1 (inc&get -2)
(this.lastThreadId = -1)
Thread B: id = 0 (inc&get -1)
(this.lastThreadId = 0)
Thread A: returns 1 (because id == -1, and this.lastThreadId=0 in the meantime)
(this.lastThreadId = 1)
Thread B: returns 0 (because id!=-1)

OK?

author nils-christian -- Fri, 7 Oct 2011 13:50:40 +0200

I am not Peer, but I took a look at the problem. It seems the problem is as follows:
Under Windows the single paths of the classpath have to be separated via a semicolon as we know. But for the Windows PowerShell the semicolon separates also single commands, which means that the PowerShell tries to "execute" the parts of the classpath.

Proposal for solution: One has to use quotation marks around the whole classpath.

If you want, I can try if this solution works for all examples or if it results in other troubles with cmd.exe.

author nils-christian -- Wed, 14 Dec 2011 16:03:20 +0100

A little problem occurred while implementing the new pipes&filters structure with annotations, due to Java reflection:
To remind again: The class AbstractPlugin is responsible for the storage of the registered methods, for the connecting of the plugins and the calling of the corresponding methods (via deliver).
The calling is a little bit problematic. The visibility modifiers / access restriction cannot be annulled. This means that the method to be invoked have to be public, but, which is even more important, must also be visible for the AbstractPlugin. This means that classes like the FilesystemLogReplayer are problematic, because they use intern (respectively package-visible) classes (like in this case the RecordDelegationPlugin), which are not visible for AbstractPlugin and whose methods can therefore not be called.

The question is: What to do now? In my opinion the best approach would be to extract and generalize the delegator classes in question sooner or later. What do you think?

author Jan Waller -- Wed, 14 Dec 2011 16:18:23 +0100

So, these classes should use public instead of private, package or protected?

Alternatively, call setAccessible(true) to ignore the restrictions. In case of the AnalysisComponent, we assume no SecurityManager preventing the access. (It is already used in AbstractMonitoringRecord.)

author André van Hoorn -- Fri, 20 Jan 2012 12:44:50 +0100

The following script unifies trace ids contained in monitoring logs.

Please note:
1. It is assumed that the log contains only OperationExecutionRecords
1. This concerns only Kieker4COM-based logs and not those obtained from Java or .NET systems

#!/bin/bash

# Add an offset to each traceid. 
# Each log has a unique offset

LOG_DIRS=$(ls -d /MY/LOG/BASE/DIR/* | grep "kieker-")
LOG_DIRS=$(echo ${LOG_DIRS} | tr "\n" " ")

TRACE_ID_OFFSET=1000000
CUR_TRACE_BASE=0
for d in ${LOG_DIRS}; do
    CUR_TRACE_BASE=$((${CUR_TRACE_BASE}+${TRACE_ID_OFFSET}))
    echo "${d}/ (current offset=${CUR_TRACE_BASE})"
    for f in ${d}/*.dat; do 
        cat $f \
            | awk -F";" \
              -v OFFSET=${CUR_TRACE_BASE} \
              '{ print $1";"$2";"$3";"$4";"$5";"$6+OFFSET";"$7";"$8";"$9";"$10";"$11 }' \
            > /tmp/tmp.dat
        cp /tmp/tmp.dat $f
    done
done

public static final String CONFIG_MAX_TRACE_DURATION_MILLIS = "maxTraceDurationMillis";

instead of 

#!java
public static final String CONFIG_MAX_TRACE_DURATION_MILLIS = 
     EventRecordTraceGenerationFilter.class.getName() + ".maxTraceDurationMillis";

Hence, the plugin name property can be a static constant in the abstract super class.

author Marius Löwe -- Thu, 6 Sep 2012 06:38:59 +0200

OperationExecutionWebRequestRegistrationInterceptor can be added this way:

    <mvc:interceptors>
        <bean class="kieker.monitoring.probe.spring.executions.OperationExecutionWebRequestRegistrationInterceptor" />
    </mvc:interceptors>

OperationExecutionMethodInvocationInterceptor can be added this way:

    <bean id="opEMII" class="kieker.monitoring.probe.spring.executions.OperationExecutionMethodInvocationInterceptor" />
 
    <aop:config>
        <aop:advisor advice-ref="opEMII" pointcut="execution(public * kieker.examples.userguide.spring.Bookstore.searchBook(..))"/>
    </aop:config>

This way the interceptor is registered for calls to the searchBook method.

I think the latter interceptor could also be added via org.springframework.aop.framework.ProxyFactoryBean but in a short test it didn't worked as expected.

Bei der Verwendung von Kieker in Serie 1 und 5 sind wir streng nach der Anleitung vorgegangen. Dabei traten für Aufgabe 1 keine nennenswerten Probleme auf. Das Einbetten in Eclipse als Jar-Datei war komfortabel, der Import in den annotierten Klassen verständlich.

Etwas seltsam war das Erstellen der Konfigurationsdateien. Diese lagen im Kieker-Zip, dass man herunterladen konnte soweit wir uns erinnern nicht in einem Verzeichnis, wie das, welches man zum Kompilieren benötigt, sondern in mehreren Verzeichnissen. Das zusammensuchen der Demo-Konfiguration ist also verbesserungswürdig.

Bei der Verwendung für Aufgabe 5 dachten wir zunächst, wir könnten die Konfiguration 1:1 übernehmen, allerdings gab es dann folgende Fehlermeldung:

Mai 28, 2012 10:47:49 PM kieker.monitoring.writer.AbstractAsyncWriter newMonitoringRecord
Schwerwiegend: Failed to retrieve new monitoring record.
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Queue full
at java.util.AbstractQueue.add(Unknown Source)
at java.util.concurrent.ArrayBlockingQueue.add(Unknown Source)
at kieker.monitoring.writer.AbstractAsyncWriter.newMonitoringRecord(AbstractAsyncWriter.java:135)
at kieker.monitoring.core.controller.WriterController.newMonitoringRecord(WriterController.java:110)
at kieker.monitoring.core.controller.MonitoringController.newMonitoringRecord(MonitoringController.java:202)
at kieker.monitoring.probe.aspectj.operationExecution.AbstractOperationExecutionAspect.operation(AbstractOperationExecutionAspect.java:92)
at stacks.Stack.pop(Stack.java:92)
at misc.runMe$StackOperator.run(runMe.java:28)

Wie in der Fehlermeldung beschrieben ist die queue voll. In der Konfigurationsdatei gibt es aber zum Glück die Option, das Verhalten bei voller Queue festzulegen. Der sprechende Name der Option, und die Kommentierung sorgten dafür, dass nicht einmal ein Blick ins Handbuch erforderlich war, um ein Ausführen zu ermöglichen. kieker.monitoring.writer.filesystem.AsyncFsWriter.QueueFullBehavior=1 sorgt zwar dafür, dass die Ausführung temporär angehalten wird, um die queue zu leeren, aber das spielt bei der Demoanwendung in der Übungsaufgabe ja keine Rolle (nicht zeitkritisch).

author André van Hoorn -- Tue, 3 Jul 2012 14:25:29 +0200

Added an initial version of the filter in changeset:629a118a3327aa3849a45a6e7b8bdac907cf5d05/kieker-git:

  • Filter class: kieker.analysis.plugin.filter.forward.RealtimeRecordDelayFilter
  • Test class: kieker.test.analysis.junit.plugin.filter.forward.TestRealtimeRecordDelayFilter

Currently,

  • the filter schedules incoming IMonitoringRecord's based on their logging timestamps for later forwarding via its output port.
  • it maintains the current time based on the latest timestamp observed so far.
  • before termination, the filter awaits the latest scheduled record to be processed.
  • the ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor is configured to use a single worker thread.
  • the precision of the internal timer is milliseconds.

I'd suggest to have a review of the API before closing the ticket.

Filter class: kieker.analysis.plugin.filter.forward.CountingThroughputFilter
Test class: kieker.test.analysis.junit.plugin.filter.forward.TestCountingThroughputFilter

Currently,

  • the filter counts the number of incoming observed in consecutive time intervals
  • it provides two input ports (not to be used together):

    1. for IMonitoringRecord's where the logging timestamp is used as the time value

    2. for Object's where the current time is used as the time value

  • it provides the list of counts per intervals via the method getCountsPerInterval

I'd suggest to have a review of the API before closing the ticket.

Fixed these 3 filters in changeset:9aa82efb136e40d685a4a445c05da862e6a32d00/kieker-git

The default files, written to the working directory, are now:

  1. executionTraces-yyyymmdd-hhmmsssSSS.txt
    2. invalidTraceArtifacts-yyyymmdd-hhmmsssSSS.txt
    3. messageTraces-yyyymmdd-hhmmsssSSS.txt
    With yyyymmdd-hhmmsssSSS being the date/time when getDefaultConfiguration is invoked by the framework.

Example implementation from ExecutionTraceWriterFilter:

#!java
	Override
	protected Configuration getDefaultConfiguration() {
		final DateFormat date = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyMMdd'-'HHmmssSSS", Locale.US);
		date.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC"));
		final String dateStr = date.format(new java.util.Date()); // NOPMD (Date)
		final String defaultFn = Constants.EXECUTION_TRACES_FN_PREFIX + "-" + dateStr + ".txt";

		final Configuration configuration = new Configuration();
		configuration.setProperty(CONFIG_PROPERTY_NAME_OUTPUT_FN, defaultFn);
		return configuration;
	}

author nils-christian -- Sun, 17 Mar 2013 09:47:20 +0100

The problem should be solved with changeset:1654097c69cfc6b3dbeda09265b96fb7fed81353kieker.webgui. At least libraries can be removed/replaced and projects can be removed.

Technically I already solved the problem earlier, as I don't convert the class objects into meta model instances every time the user wants to add a plugin to the graph anymore. Instead I convert all of them when the application starts or the libraries of a project are changed. The beans responsible for modifying their project meta models get a list of available plugins/repositories as meta model instances (prototype design pattern).

As this seems to solve the underlying problem, I close this ticket and mark it as fixed.

Edit: It could be possible that this problem will later occur again, when the cockpit uses the methods of a running analysis. If this should be the case, reopen this ticket.

Edit: Another problem is that the lock objects of removed projects are not removed as well. This could, for example, be solved by checking the lock objects for correctness after they have been locked.

author nils-christian -- Fri, 2 Nov 2012 19:47:23 +0100

The classloader issue will be solved as following:
1) Every request for a new classloader (when a user opens a project) has to be done by leaving the (weak) reference to the requester.
2) Every request for a new classloader will be done by copying the available libraries of a project to a temporary directory which will then be used by the new classloader.
3) Once one of the requesters will be released (by the GC), the manager (as an observable) will be informed so that it can run through the still open classloaders and (if the requester doesn't exist any longer) can close them (and it can remove the temporary directory as well). This is necessary as the PreDestroy annotation doesn't work correctly for view scoped beans.
4) As the close() method of the URLClassLoader isn't available in 1.6, I will use a hack to implement this behavior. This will (probably) only work on Sun VMs.

It seems like the OutOfMemoryError can still occur, but it is much less likely. I will look into this later.

author nils-christian -- Mon, 5 Nov 2012 09:02:01 +0100

The described behavior has been implemented in changeset:18c0eefc795e35eceb276e4807a38130c4d7c3d3/kieker.webgui. As there doesn't seem to be a "good" way to create temporary directories in Java 1.6, I decided to use a self-managed temporary directory. I use a simple counter to find a valid directory. When the corresponding classloader is closed, the directory is removed as well. Furthermore the responsible bean tries to clean the whole temporary directory when it is disposed.

The direct access to the FS is still not a good behavior for a web application and is therefore also related to KIEKER-822 Done .

I close this ticket, as the changes solve the classloader issue. It is still possible that the OutOfMemoryError can occur. I "solved" this by increasing the memory space (-XX:PermSize=256M -XX:MaxPermSize=512M -Xms128M -Xmx256M) and to give the GC therefore the time to work.

author nils-christian -- Mon, 3 Dec 2012 00:24:21 +0100

As an additional comment:
The problem can still occur if one
- for example
- opens a lot of projects and closes them very fast one after another. This is because a lot of classloaders will be opened and the GC can't handle this very good. I solved this by making sure that classloaders will only be created in the following situations:
- The FS manager starts (during the application start itself) and initializes the projects
- A project is created or a library for a project is uploaded/removed (this is necessary because additional libraries could also change specific characteristics of the plugin/repository classes itself (JMXReader as an example)
- An analysis is initialized

Except during the above mentioned situations, no additional classloader will be created. The FS manager loads the available components (as model instances) for every projects and sends them to the beans which needs them. The beans can then copy the available components to create new instances of them.
It is technically still possible to overload the PermGen space if one adds a lot of libraries or removes a lot of them, but at least it is not possible to overload the space by reloading a lot of pages anymore. A test with JMeter looked very good to me.

I implemented this behavior in changeset:6af3e84de8ec5b6043ecd6288a88bc0e1d747d6b/kieker.webgui. I still have to test whether all classloaders will be disposed correctly though.

We have the following problems with our current (programmtic) API:

  • The same filter could be registered to more than one AnalysisController (should be prevented! We have controllers with state!)
  • We have no concept of project, but the Analysis Controller (and we have the project name as a constructor argument), so the project configuration should belong to the AnalysisController.
  • The filters are configured in their constructors (vie the Configuration argument).
  • at this time, there is no connection between a filter and its project (analysis controller)
  • this connection is created when a filter is registered (and we could add project properties at this time), but this prevents the use of, e.g, final variables.

The better solution would be (in my opinion) to change the filter constructor to new(Configuration, AnalysisController), thus fixing both problem (but breaking the API).

author 557058:4d47b709-5ab9-428d-9914-3145699aac95 unknown Jira user -- Fri, 14 Dec 2012 13:37:50 +0100

OSGi is a multi-ClassLoader environment which means that every OSGi-bundle has its own ClassLoader. Additionally there is a top-level ClassLoader which is used for running the OSGi Framework itself. Just an example why Kieker does not work out-of-the-box in this environment:

Let's assume we have two OSGi Bundles BundleA and BundleB with the following classes:
BundleA:
- ClassA1
- ClassA2
BundleB:
- ClassB1
- ClassB2

The corresponding ClassLoader structure looks like this:
- ClassLoader-TL (top-level)


- ClassLoader-A (BundleA)


- ClassLoader-B (BundleB)

If we want to instrument ClassA1 for example, and we just start the JVM with the AspectJ agent as argument (as we would do it for plain Java applications) the Kieker-Instrumentation does not work.
Why? Because AspectJ uses ClassLoader-TL for code-weaving. However, this class loader does not know the class ClassA1. For classes of BundleA ClassLoader-A has to be used for code weaving, respectively for BundleB.

  • DBReader: Thread-Safe as the only field which can be set (running) is volatile.

author nils-christian -- Tue, 19 Feb 2013 20:54:18 +0100

The good news: It is surprisingly easy to write an own checkstyle check.

The bad news: According to the checkstyle project page (http://checkstyle.sourceforge.net/writingchecks.html) there are some limitations like

  • "You cannot determine the type of an expression."
  • "You cannot see the content of other files. (although you can save processed files for use later)"

That means it is not really possible to do what we want to do:

  • Check whether a given class extends directly or indirectly the AnalysisComponent
  • Check whether the class supplies the correct constructor

However, what I can do is the following:

  • Check whether a class has an annotation with an identifier named "Plugin" or "Repository" (which means both false positives and false negatives)
  • Check whether a class has a constructor which gets two parameters with types named "Configuration" and "IProjectContext".

I think that could already be enough. My simple first attempt found most of the listened classes in KIEKER-787 Done .

If that is enough, we can easily use it. Question is: Where do I put the source file?

Furthermore I want to explain in some few words how to write a simple checkstyle check in case anybody needs this:

  • Extend the class com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.api.Check
  • Implement the method getDefaultTokens to show which tokens should be checked (classes, constructors, ...)
  • Implement the method visitToken which will be called for each of the defined tokens. Using the token you can work within the whole tree of the source code file.
  • Use this.log to report a found rule violation

Replying to KIEKER-887 Done :
> Inspired by KIEKER-369 Done
>
> We should remove compile time libraries from the binary release.
> There is no real reason to deliver them inside it?

Sure, if libs are solely needed for the build, we can skip them (e.g., maven-ant-tasks-2.1.3.jar). However, I don't see many others. For most of the libs, I see this as a convenience of the release to provide the runtime libs in the right version. Otherwise, users would need to manually search for them (e.g., the right CXF/Spring libs) --- which is quite cumbersome due to the inter-dependencies.

> Furthermore, we should check which libraries are really needed, e.g., is log4j still needed?

We are using log4j mainly to redirect log output to a file kieker.log in the CLI scripts (see also KIEKER-369 Done ). However, this should also be possible with the JDK logger. All we need is a running configuration (file).

author André van Hoorn -- Mon, 2 Sep 2013 14:58:57 +0200

Replying to [avh|comment:4]:
> Check whether add is called after getTraceAsSortedExecutionSet

The add and getTraceAsSortedExecutionSet methods are currently called from the following places:

  • TraceReconstructionFilter. The inputExecutions method creates ExecutionTrace objects and put them to pendingTraces and timeoutMap Maps. For each new Execution, The TraceReconstructionFilter looks up the corresponding ExecutionTrace (if existent, by trace ID) from the pendingTraces map and (if present) removes it from the timeoutMap. The removal from the timeoutMap involves a Comparator<ExecutionTrace>, which uses the getTraceAsSortedExecutionSet method to access the tin property of the first execution in the returned execution set. A call to getTraceAsSortedExecutionSet could be avoided here by providing a dedicated method for the earliest tin in an ExecutionTrace. But the situation seems fine. The add method is used to add the Execution to the ExecutionTrace (which is newly created if lookup failed). Conclusion for this class: Mixed use of add and getTraceAsSortedExecutionSet --- the latter being called very frequently as part of the map lookups.
  • ExecutionTraceHashContainerAllocationEquivalence and ExecutionTraceHashContainerAssemblyEquivalence. These classes are used in the TraceEquivalenceClassFilter and call the getTraceAsSortedExecutionSet once at construction time to construct a hash code but potentially more frequently as part of the equals method (in case the hash key matches). However, for the latter, I don't really see why the ExecutionTrace's equals method is not used ...
  • In various tests, the getTraceAsSortedExecutionSet method is used to obtain the set of Execution}}s from the complete (i.e., no more {{Execution}}s will be added) from the {{ExecutionTrace. Hence, for each ExecutionTrace a copy would be created once.

author nils-christian -- Sat, 20 Apr 2013 09:30:59 +0200

Done in 545d91d82d4ea5f98e0c0ffe9993e19b28dffd92.

From the javadoc:

This plugin provides the current (system) time in regular intervals. The time is delivered to the two output ports as both a timestamp and a {link TimestampRecord} instance.

The reader can be configured to be either blocking or non-blocking. In the first mode the read-method doesn't return and waits instead for a call to the terminate method. In the second mode the read method does return immediately, resulting in the termination of the whole analysis, if no other reader exists.

The sent timestamps are created using {link System#nanoTime()} as a time source, which is being converted to the global time unit (as defined in the configuration from the given {link IProjectContext}).

Currently the tests are not perfect, e.g. the test assumes that the non-blocking mode returns within 5 seconds. Technically this assumption could fail (although it is not very likely). As it is just a test, I think it is okay. If the test tends to fail, I rework it.

author nils-christian -- Mon, 20 May 2013 16:18:27 +0200

Should be solved with changeset:b610e3f7fd27a52d6b58cd2bc0c1e4722432f056/kieker.webgui.

1. I removed the redundant jar file of Kieker. Instead I used a maven plugin (maven-dependency-plugin) to download the kieker dependency and copy it directly during the compile phase into the correct directory. As I rename the jar file to kieker.jar during this process, the FSManager and the two tests just have to know the name kieker.jar
- independent from the actual kieker version.
1. The maven war plugin (which is uses to assemble the war file) provides the possibility to "filter" files and replace, for example, property place holders with actual values. I used this possibility to let the version tag within the about dialog replace with the actual version during the package phase. This means that the version string is empty, if one uses jetty:run to compile and start the web application. But during the correct package phase (which is used during the nightly build e.g.) the value is correctly set and appears within the dialog.

To cut a long story short: If one wants to change the version number, it is sufficient to change it within the pom.xml (If the Kieker version changes, this has to be changed as well, of course. Currently twice within the pom, but I will see if I can change this as well).

author nils-christian -- Fri, 3 May 2013 15:26:37 +0200

Replying to [jwa|comment:1]:
> ConcurrentHashMaps are not synchronized and usually a quite good implementation, even for single threaded access.

Yes, but why waste time? If I look into the implementation, I still see volatile fields and locks which are both unnecessary for our case.

Maybe we could make a simple test setup (outside Kieker) and compare the performance of those maps? Or maybe those implementations have already been compared?

> But this could be evaluated further.
> Collections.unmodificable* is just another API redirection removing the methods.

True. Would probably only slow the operations down.

author Jan Waller -- Fri, 3 May 2013 15:33:31 +0200

The possible problem is not locking or synchronization, but visibility.
The data structure is accessed from more than one thread (at least it will be in the future), so it requires some mechanimn to ensure full visibility (e.g., final, synchronized, volatile, ...)
It is a dynamically sized structure, so we can't declare each field final. Such a data structure provides the usually the best and safest access.

We should rather check this for all other fields accessed by more than one thread ...

Speed:
ConcurrentHashMap reads a volatile var upon access. Reading a volatile var has the same cost (on most systems) as reading a normal var (it only prevents some reordering). Writing a volatile var is expensive, but only happens when the structure is changed, so in our case never.

author rju -- Mon, 6 May 2013 13:35:28 +0200

I concur with jwa to test the configuration parameter for null. However, I find the modification of the configuration inside constructor problematic. For example, if I have a default configuration already assigned to the configuration it will be overwritten. Even if the change of this construct results in sublime API changes, it will result in code which is better to comprehend. The passed configuration should be final (in a sense of not being manipulated), but the present approach breaks that logic.

What is the benefit of the present approach?

In the Configuration class, the setDefaultConfiguration is quite an interesting function. First, its comment states that it is a workaround to implement writers. And it only sets the default configuration, if no default configuration has been set. In the other case it will produce an either an IllegalAccessException if the default configuration is set again with a new default configuration. If the "new" default configuration is null then nothing happens.

While this is a little weird, it is definitely not a good choice to be called in a constructor of a component depending on configuration.

author nils-christian -- Sat, 14 Sep 2013 22:26:16 +0200

Realized a problem which could be the possible cause of the whole issue. It seems like each newly loaded and created AC also creates a thread. This could be the reason why the GC cannot unload the classes. The threads are named "EMF Reference Cleaner". It seems like the EMF starts a daemon thread to clean the references when we load a KAX file.

The daemon thread itself seems to run in an infinite loop. It is also created as local variable. Makes it difficult to send an interrupt signal or something to the thread.

Edit: I found a possibility to interrupt the correct thread. However, this is not a good solution. We should discuss further solutions.

author rju -- Thu, 31 Oct 2013 15:07:48 +0100

Further analysis showed that the meta-API (the structural approach, which the API follows) is more diverse than expected, as a wide range of interfaces is used, which do not follow the taxonomic structure of class inheritance. Interfaces are used to describe common properties of records and to mark records. Both features must be understood completely before progress can be made for the IRL. Furthermore, the information is necessary for future documentation of Kieker.

As a first step, 36 different record types have been checked. The list of class signatures can be found in the attachment. An aggregated list of these types looks like:

#!java
public abstract class AbstractMonitoringRecord implements IMonitoringRecord
public class *                                 extends AbstractMonitoringRecord implements IMonitoringRecord.Factory, IMonitoringRecord.BinaryFactory
public class TraceMetadata                     extends AbstractMonitoringRecord implements IMonitoringRecord.Factory, IMonitoringRecord.BinaryFactory, IFlowRecord
public abstract class AbstractEvent            extends AbstractMonitoringRecord implements IMonitoringRecord.Factory, IMonitoringRecord.BinaryFactory, IEventRecord
public abstract class AbstractTraceEvent       extends AbstractEvent implements ITraceRecord
public class *                                 extends AbstractTraceEvent
public abstract class AbstractMonitorEvent     extends AbstractTraceEvent
public class ConstructionEvent                 extends AbstractTraceEvent implements IObjectRecord
public class *                                 extends AbstractMonitorEvent
public abstract class AbstractOperationEvent   extends AbstractTraceEvent implements IOperationRecord
public class *                                 extends AbstractOperationEvent
public class CallOperationEvent                extends AbstractOperationEvent implements ICallRecord
public class BeforeOperationObjectEvent        extends BeforeOperationEvent implements IObjectRecord
public class BeforeConstructorEvent            extends BeforeOperationEvent implements IConstructorRecord
public class CallOperationObjectEvent          extends CallOperationEvent implements ICallObjectRecord
public class AfterOperationObjectEvent         extends AfterOperationEvent implements IObjectRecord
public class AfterOperationFailedEvent         extends AfterOperationEvent implements IExceptionRecord
public class AfterConstructorEvent             extends AfterOperationEvent implements IConstructorRecord
public class AfterOperationFailedObjectEvent   extends AfterOperationFailedEvent implements IObjectRecord
public class AfterConstructorFailedEvent       extends AfterOperationFailedEvent implements IConstructorRecord
public class CallConstructorEvent              extends CallOperationEvent implements IConstructorRecord

Will be continued later.
