author rju -- Thu, 31 Oct 2013 17:42:01 +0100

The list of classes contains several interfaces which fall in two groups:

  1. Real interfaces implementing common interfaces which require multiple inheritance
  2. Marker interfaces

Marker interfaces are normally used to 'tag' something, which could be achieved with annotations. However, this was not the case in Kieker for, I guess, Java 1.4 compatibility reasons.

The interfaces are:

  • IMonitoringRecord : general record interface
    • IFlowRecord : Marker interface, distinguish flow from other record types
      • ITraceRecord : trace data
      • IEventRecord : event data, timestamp
      • IExceptionRecord : exception cause
      • IObjectRecord : describes one object
        • ICallObjectRecord :
      • IOperationRecord : describes one operation
        • IConstructorRecord : Marker interface, distinguishes constructors from other operations
        • ICallRecord : Descibing operation calls
  • ICallObjectRecord : ??? This adds new functionality, but uses still ICallRecord and IObjectRecord. Ins't there some duplication?
  • IMonitoringRecord.Factory : Marker interface

The only multi inheritance interface is ICallObjectRecord, but many AbstractMonitoringRecord descendants implement various interfaces.

In general, these interfaces could be seen as partial descriptions of records even though they do not provide record infrastructure. In the IRL these could be represented by special template structures.

What i do not understand are the factory interfaces:

  • IMonitoringRecord.Factory
  • IMonitoringRecord.BinaryFactory

IMHO they only allows to mark that a record supports special initialization, serialization or deserialization methods. But IMonitoringRecord already requires all these methods to be compulsory. Would it not be more coherent to either place the necessary methods in those Factory interfaces or move those methods to other interfaces, which can then be included separately.

If they are only used to test if a record provides these capabilities, we could drop them in a generated record environment, because all records will have or have not these features depending on the generator implementation.

author Jan Waller -- Thu, 31 Oct 2013 17:49:53 +0100

Evaluating Annotations is expensive compared to check for interface implementation.

Implementing the Factory Interfaces requires additional constriants (e.g., static fields) that are not enforceable by interfaces. The methods also work without these interfaces but with a different underlying implementation (that is less performant). This should all be documented in the relevant JavaDoc.

author rju -- Mon, 4 Nov 2013 10:35:12 +0100

I know an isAnnotationPresent or getAnnotation call requires approx. twice the time of getClass.equals or instanceof. However, those annotations play only a role on the analysis side and would therefore only delay the analysis.

Still I do not understand the necessity of the interfaces IMonitoringRecord.Factory and IMonitoringRecord.BinaryFactory, as they appear to be in all records. If everything is marked, they could be omitted and the tooling can assume the semantics attached to these interfaces. Of course they do not introduce additional problems in code generation, as placing them everywhere does not complicate things.

Other marker interfaces also carry semantics. But it is unclear what their semantics are. An easy fix would be to allow interface declarations in the IRL, but that would not be optimal, as the semantics of the interfaces would be obscured. In the present Kieker implementation, they are used to provide common interfaces and sometimes as markers. For a DSL design it is helpful to know what kind of property do they mark, and what the common interface calls describe.

The problem seems to be that the PreMain method is executed too early in the classloading process. The moment we perform our check not all classloaders have been loaded. Therefore we might not be able to detect an existing AOP configuration file in a multi-classloader environment (OSGI, JavaEE, ...).

Possible solutions:
1. Remove our aop-config-file detection feature
1. Provide a fourth jar file containing AspectJ and usable only in standalone environments
1. Use the command line argument in multi-classloader environments
1. Try to detect whether the PreMain is executed in a JavaEE/OSGI environment

author Thomas F. Düllmann -- Tue, 17 Jun 2014 14:23:45 +0200

Replying to [jwa|comment:3]:
> Is this still topical?

The current state is that R is installed on the CI-Server and it is started by a script that is triggered by the build script. For one build instance using Rserve this works quite well, but there may be issues with multiple build instances running concurrently as Rserve can't be gracefully stopped (instead we use pkill for now).

So when there is more than one build using the Rserve-scripts they may kill eachothers Rserve instances.

To make this more resilient even for more than one concurrently running build using Rserve, some classes within the opad-tslib-integration branch would have to be rewritten (especially RBridgeControl -> e.g. configuration options for Port number).

author André van Hoorn -- Wed, 25 Jun 2014 15:28:08 +0200

Implemented and used in CI environment.

Current limitation of the bin/dev/rserve-control.sh: termination of server using pkill, which call all running rserve instances, i.e., not only the one started by the script (haven't seen a good solution so far).

Thomas: Please create a ticket for this issue (e.g., store PID when starting and kill only this PID. However, currently we start on the default port and the script can only start once before stop).

author Thomas F. Düllmann -- Wed, 25 Jun 2014 17:22:11 +0200

Perhaps a graceful start/stop of Rserve could be done with start-stop-daemon.
See: https://code.google.com/p/rsession/source/browse/wiki/RserveLinuxDaemon.wiki

issue.body:
JIRA Issue: [KIEKER-1050] Enhance/extend Kieker's analysis framework Original Reporter: Andre van Hoorn ***

To be polished

Brief explanation:

  • (Max. 5-7 sentences)
  • Kieker's analysis component includes convenient framework to develop analyses based on pipes-and-filters style
  • Nice to have:
  • Composite components
  • Event-based analysis as an alternative to pipes-and-filters
  • Cleaned up TraceAnalysis "god class"

Related tickets:

  • KIEK-555: Feature wish: Analysis server back-end architecture
  • KIEKER-519 Done , KIEKER-218 Done , ...: Cleaned up TraceAnalysis tool
  • #806: Feature wish: Support for composite filters
  • KIEK-832: Feature wish: Integrate complex event processing engine
  • KIEK-848: Feature wish: Support for distributed analysis configurations

Expected results:

  • 2-3 sentences

Knowledge prerequisite:

  • List skills (programming language, technologies, etc.) nice to have and mention that they may be gained during the project (if applicable)

Skill level:

Additional documentation

  • Maybe some links to information on technologies, papers, etc.

Mentor(s):

  • [André van Hoorn|Kieker:author/avh/]

  • Nils Ehmke?

The parameter -d of the program xargs specifies the delimiter for the given list
- in this case a newline character. However, the manual of Solaris' xargs tells the following:

Arguments  in  the  standard  input  must  be  separated  by
unquoted  blank characters, or unescaped blank characters or
newline characters.

The parameter is therefore not needed under Solaris.

body: We seem to have an issue with merging this branch and main. Some issues are in Java files that do not follow the code style of Kieker.
Usually this should not lead to a merge conflict. Also the merge conflict of the binary files is new. I do not know why we get this.
@rju Thank you for having a look. The merge is mostly about gradle script/binary updates. I can disard this pull request and prepare a new one from the current main. Does this make sense to you?

Doing this all over again is one option, the probably easier option is manually rebasing. 

So first, I pulled the newest commits of `main` and `KIEKER-1996-UpdateToGradle8-9`, checked out `KIEKER-1996-UpdateToGradle8-9`, and did `git rebase main`. Now, the merge conflicts occured.

To fix them, for every conflict, we need to checkout the branch version, for example `git checkout KIEKER-1996-UpdateToGradle8-9 -- examples/JavaEEServletContainerExample/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar` 

To do this with every changed file, I did `git status | grep "von beiden geändert" | awk -F':' '{print $2}' | xargs git checkout KIEKER-1996-UpdateToGradle8-9 -- $1` (parsing the German git output - so please set your OS to German for this one ;-) ). 

Now, I pushed to this branch with `--force`, and it builds again. If this is successful, we can merge.

And I wouldn't expect errors in Java files `git diff main --name-only | grep java` is empty...

issue.title: [KIEKER-1978] Document / Fix Spring Monitoring

repository.name: kieker
repository.description: Kieker is an observability framework, that consists of an monitoring and tracing agent, and compatible analysis tools

issue.body:
JIRA Issue: [KIEKER-1978] Document / Fix Spring Monitoring Original Reporter: David Georg Reichelt ***

Currently, I’m trying to get Micro-company (https://github.com/idugalic/micro-company ) running with Kieker. This is a microservice example application that has been used in some case studies.

Unfortunately, monitoring does not work and Kiekers slf4j-versions block logging, so I also do not get any error messages. After building my fork (https://github.com/DaGeRe/micro-company ) on the master branch (mvn clean install -DskipTests), the application can be started regularly in monolithic/target/docker using java -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher.

Adding the javaagent with default configurations ends with no logs:

java -javaagent:kieker-1.15.4-aspectj.jar -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher

SLF4J: Failed to load class "org.slf4j.impl.StaticLoggerBinder".
SLF4J: Defaulting to no-operation (NOP) logger implementation
SLF4J: See http://www.slf4j.org/codes.html#StaticLoggerBinder for further details.

and with a lot of logging data, that are only spring of logback data:

reicheltreichelt-desktop:~/nvme/workspaces/kiekerworkspace/micro-company/monolithic/target/docker$ cat /tmp/kieker-20240315-144756-21219659539625-UTC--KIEKER-SINGLETON/kieker*dat | wc -l
7928688

These records are mostly spring-internal things, e.g., org.springframework.boot.loader.jar.JarFileEntries.swap

After these ~7 million records, nothing happens (no more kieker entries, no response from the application via http, no logs). The application is not started in this configuration, so for some reason, adding the javaagent to a spring application in this context stops the spring application from being executed.

To overcome this, I tried to only instrument the idugalic package thing, with the following kieker.aop.xml:

<!DOCTYPE aspectj PUBLIC "-//AspectJ//DTD//EN" "http://www.aspectj.org/dtd/aspectj_1_5_0.dtd">
<aspectj>
{{ <weaver options="-verbose">}}
{{ <include within="com.idugalic..*" />}}
{{ </weaver>}}
{{ <aspects>}}
{{ <aspect}}
{{ name="kieker.monitoring.probe.aspectj.operationExecution.OperationExecutionAspectFull" />}}
{{ </aspects>}}
</aspectj>

Using this, the application is functional from the outside, but still does not get logs (not even /tmp/kieker-XYZ is created - logfile is attached).

For debugging the AspectJ behavior, I think its necessary to get the logging right. Unfortunately, spring (or the 1.5.3 version, which is used here) does not work together with Kieker, even when just adding Kieker to the classpath (java -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar:kieker-1.15.4-aspectj.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher), the logging stops to work. Also adding the slf4j and logback libraries in the version that are normally used (java -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar:BOOT-INF/lib/slf4j-api-1.7.25.jar:BOOT-INF/lib/logback-core-1.1.11.jar:BOOT-INF/lib/logback-classic-1.1.11.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher) does not fix this problem.

According to new relic, adding a javaagent directly to spring should just work (https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apm/agents/java-agent/additional-installation/include-java-agent-jvm-argument/ ), the documentation about spring instrumentation with Kieker is unfortunately empty (https://kieker-monitoring.readthedocs.io/en/latest/instrumenting-software/java/Instrumentation-of-Spring.html ).

Is there any way to get Kieker runnable with an older slf4j / spring version, and if yes, how?

[KIEKER-1978]: https://kieker-monitoring.atlassian.net/browse/KIEKER-1978?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

```
	at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:579)
	at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.ClassLoaders$AppClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoaders.java:178)
	at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:522)
	at java.base/java.lang.Class.forName0(Native Method)
	at java.base/java.lang.Class.forName(Class.java:398)
	at java.base/sun.launcher.LauncherHelper.loadMainClass(LauncherHelper.java:760)
	at java.base/sun.launcher.LauncherHelper.checkAndLoadMain(LauncherHelper.java:655)
```

Unfortunately, I didn't find a way to avoid this: Ignoring `java.util` or something like this didn't work, since we need `java.util` to check whether a class matches a regular expression - if we ignore it, there are classes we need to load, for example `sun.launcher.LauncherHelper`, and we can't check whether they match the regular expressions if we didn't load something from `java.util` right now. Since I can't specify the order in which the classes are loaded, I don't know how to fix this (and I assume there is no way to fix this, without fixing it inside of ByteBuddy).

This has also been discussed inside of ByteBuddy: https://github.com/raphw/byte-buddy/issues/558 (without solution).

I'd still like to merge this PR, which now documents this behavior instead of changing it.

Update ByteBuddy to 1.15.1 and manage version in gradle.properties

issue.title: [KIEKER-1978] Document / Fix Spring Monitoring

repository.name: kieker
repository.description: Kieker is an observability framework, that consists of an monitoring and tracing agent, and compatible analysis tools

issue.body:
JIRA Issue: [KIEKER-1978] Document / Fix Spring Monitoring Original Reporter: David Georg Reichelt ***

Currently, I’m trying to get Micro-company (https://github.com/idugalic/micro-company ) running with Kieker. This is a microservice example application that has been used in some case studies.

Unfortunately, monitoring does not work and Kiekers slf4j-versions block logging, so I also do not get any error messages. After building my fork (https://github.com/DaGeRe/micro-company ) on the master branch (mvn clean install -DskipTests), the application can be started regularly in monolithic/target/docker using java -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher.

Adding the javaagent with default configurations ends with no logs:

java -javaagent:kieker-1.15.4-aspectj.jar -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher

SLF4J: Failed to load class "org.slf4j.impl.StaticLoggerBinder".
SLF4J: Defaulting to no-operation (NOP) logger implementation
SLF4J: See http://www.slf4j.org/codes.html#StaticLoggerBinder for further details.

and with a lot of logging data, that are only spring of logback data:

reicheltreichelt-desktop:~/nvme/workspaces/kiekerworkspace/micro-company/monolithic/target/docker$ cat /tmp/kieker-20240315-144756-21219659539625-UTC--KIEKER-SINGLETON/kieker*dat | wc -l
7928688

These records are mostly spring-internal things, e.g., org.springframework.boot.loader.jar.JarFileEntries.swap

After these ~7 million records, nothing happens (no more kieker entries, no response from the application via http, no logs). The application is not started in this configuration, so for some reason, adding the javaagent to a spring application in this context stops the spring application from being executed.

To overcome this, I tried to only instrument the idugalic package thing, with the following kieker.aop.xml:

<!DOCTYPE aspectj PUBLIC "-//AspectJ//DTD//EN" "http://www.aspectj.org/dtd/aspectj_1_5_0.dtd">
<aspectj>
{{ <weaver options="-verbose">}}
{{ <include within="com.idugalic..*" />}}
{{ </weaver>}}
{{ <aspects>}}
{{ <aspect}}
{{ name="kieker.monitoring.probe.aspectj.operationExecution.OperationExecutionAspectFull" />}}
{{ </aspects>}}
</aspectj>

Using this, the application is functional from the outside, but still does not get logs (not even /tmp/kieker-XYZ is created - logfile is attached).

For debugging the AspectJ behavior, I think its necessary to get the logging right. Unfortunately, spring (or the 1.5.3 version, which is used here) does not work together with Kieker, even when just adding Kieker to the classpath (java -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar:kieker-1.15.4-aspectj.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher), the logging stops to work. Also adding the slf4j and logback libraries in the version that are normally used (java -cp monolithic-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar:BOOT-INF/lib/slf4j-api-1.7.25.jar:BOOT-INF/lib/logback-core-1.1.11.jar:BOOT-INF/lib/logback-classic-1.1.11.jar org.springframework.boot.loader.JarLauncher) does not fix this problem.

According to new relic, adding a javaagent directly to spring should just work (https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apm/agents/java-agent/additional-installation/include-java-agent-jvm-argument/ ), the documentation about spring instrumentation with Kieker is unfortunately empty (https://kieker-monitoring.readthedocs.io/en/latest/instrumenting-software/java/Instrumentation-of-Spring.html ).

Is there any way to get Kieker runnable with an older slf4j / spring version, and if yes, how?

[KIEKER-1978]: https://kieker-monitoring.atlassian.net/browse/KIEKER-1978?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

issue.body:
JIRA Issue: [KIEKER-1979] Unclarities in build.gradle Original Reporter: David Georg Reichelt ***

Some things in build.gradle are unclear to me, and it might be better to remove / refactor them:

  • https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/ef88c729f1227b41c170a9b3d3e01bc052682e2e/build.gradle#L531 Why is it checker here whether Java 1.7 or 1.8 is used? Both are out to date now.
  • https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/ef88c729f1227b41c170a9b3d3e01bc052682e2e/build.gradle#L659 Why do mainJar and emfJar contain aopxml configurations? From my point of view, this should be sufficient in the aspectJJar.
  • https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/blob/ef88c729f1227b41c170a9b3d3e01bc052682e2e/build.gradle#L76 The parent build.gradle defines that the subprojects should apply the java plugin, yet this is defined again in most of the subprojects. Wouldn’t it make sense to remove these double declarations?

body:
I've updated the PR with some formatting etc. corrections. Some more formatting errors are necessary from my point of view:
- `OperationExecutionDataGatherer` is abstract, because it shouldn't be instantiated, but is no `abstract` base class for inheritance - so I'd leave it without abstract in the name
- `OperationExecutionDataGatherer` does not have `abstract` methods, since we don't have a classical `abstract` class for inheritance as well (pmd)
- The return result in `KiekerStaticContext` makes the code more readable, so I'd leave it as it is (pmd)
- `OperationExecutionDiSL` needs to be instantiable to be usable by DiSL, so I'd ignore the warning about the default constructor
- `OperationExecutionDiSL` only has `static` methods by design of DiSL, so we shouldn't change this.
- I would in general not force people to add `@Author` tags - after committing, there is no code "ownership" besides what is specified in the license (which says everybody is allowed to use the code anyhow) and we know who committed what by git anyhow. So I'd rather get rid of this rule in checkstyle completely.

Todos:
- `KiekerStaticContext`: Mark return with NOPMD / NOCS
- `OperationExecutionDiSL`: Mark `static` methods with NPMD / NOCS
- Add `@Author` tags

`bin/dev/release-check-short.sh` ends in `[info] Success.`, and there is no other release check, so I don't see what should be missing here. The `Release Check Extended` is not executed, since the condition that we're on `main` is not fullfiled, but that should be this way for a feature branch.

After removing a deprecated test, I don't see any reason why this fails. Jenkins still shows the failure: https://build.se.informatik.uni-kiel.de/view/Kieker/job/kieker-dev/job/KIEKER-1975-Update-To-Java-11/4/

Bumps [com.github.oshi:oshi-core](https://github.com/oshi/oshi) from 3.12.2 to 6.4.7.
Release notes

Sourced from com.github.oshi:oshi-core's releases.

Release 6.4.7

Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2460: Fix AIX tests for virtual/unused drives - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2480: Use sysfs as a backup for Linux power supply without udev - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2487: Improve performance of thread details query for a single process - @​dbwiddis.

Full change log

Release 6.4.6

Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2443: Include IPConnections on Mac that listen on both IPv4 and IPv6 protocols - @​rieck0.
  • #2446: Fix parsing Loongson CPU names - @​Glavo.

Full change log

Release 6.4.5

Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2421: Handle non-unique UUIDs in demo ComputerID class - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2427: Lookup hardware implementer if lscpu fails to do so - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2434: Fix Windows OS Process logic to use registry values - @​tzfun.
  • #2436: Fall back to vendor frequency on failed max on Windows - @​dbwiddis.

Full change log

Release 6.4.4

Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2407: Improve performance of Linux User and Group name queries - @​dbwiddis.

Full change log

Release 6.4.3

Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2377: Graceful fallback for macOS Process user or group name - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2393: Get threadId by syscall when gettid not available - @​silencewood.
  • #2394: Fix bit shifting in CPUID calculation - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2396: Add command-line fallbacks for udev and sysfs processor info - @​dbwiddis.

Full change log

Release 6.4.2

Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2361: Convert per-process CPU ticks on Apple Silicon to milliseconds - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2362: Make use of Kstat2 configurable - @​dbwiddis.

Full change log

Release 6.4.1

Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2292: Update to JNA 5.13.0 - @​dbwiddis.

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from com.github.oshi:oshi-core's changelog.

6.4.0 (2022-12-02), 6.4.1 (2023-03-18), 6.4.2 (2023-05-02), 6.4.3 (2023-06-06), 6.4.4 (2023-07-01), 6.4.5 (2023-08-20), 6.4.6 (2023-09-24), 6.4.7 (2023-11-01)

New Features
  • #2261: Add getThreadId, getCurrentThread and getCurrentProcess to OperatingSystem API - @​dbwiddis.
Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2259: Cache AIX partition list to reduce disk reads from lspv - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2260: Use regex to pre-filter to parseable CPU numbers for ARM Macs - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2262: Consistent treatment of AIX tick lengths - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2264: Don't assume ticks match logical processor count - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2292: Update to JNA 5.13.0 - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2315, #2318: Fix parsing generally and for FreeBSD cpu detection - @​decketron.
  • #2327: Improve Udev exception handling - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2329: Allow using SLF4J 1 in OSGi containers - @​mshabarov.
  • #2361: Convert per-process CPU ticks on Apple Silicon to milliseconds - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2362: Make use of Kstat2 configurable - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2377: Graceful fallback for macOS Process user or group name - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2393: Get threadId by syscall when gettid not available - @​silencewood.
  • #2394: Fix bit shifting in CPUID calculation - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2396: Add command-line fallbacks for udev and sysfs processor info - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2407: Improve performance of Linux User and Group name queries - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2421: Handle non-unique UUIDs in demo ComputerID class - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2427: Lookup hardware implementer if lscpu fails to do so - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2434: Fix Windows OS Process logic to use registry values - @​tzfun.
  • #2436: Fall back to vendor frequency on failed max on Windows - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2443: Include IPConnections on macOS that listen on both IPv4 and IPv6 protocols - @​rieck0.
  • #2446: Fix parsing Loongson CPU names - @​Glavo.
  • #2460: Fix AIX tests for virtual/unused drives - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2480: Use sysfs as a backup for Linux power supply without udev - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2487: Improve performance of thread details query for a single process - @​dbwiddis.

6.3.0 (2022-10-16), 6.3.1 (2022-10-30), 6.3.2 (2022-11-16)

New Features
  • #2129: Added JMX demo project - @​SalvadorRomo.
  • #2197: Added support for Android OS - @​milan-fabian.
  • #2198: Added Processor Cache Information - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2218: Added system-wide per-process open file descriptor limits - @​gitseti
  • #2225: Added process specific open file descriptor limits - @​gitseti
Bug fixes / Improvements
  • #2179: Update JUnit EnabledOnOS for OpenBSD and FreeBSD - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2180: Suppress log warnings for common non-root procfs failures - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2181: Better handling of ARM CPU Names - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2204: Improve performance using parallel streams for processes and threads - @​adrian-kong.
  • #2212: Suppress log warnings for common non-root macOS sysctl failures - @​pavangole.
  • #2224: Detect Windows Server 2022 in older JDKs - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2229: Fix division by zero on AIX with fewer logical processors than physical processors - @​dbwiddis.
  • #2243: Actually return Windows IP Connections - @​dbwiddis.

- java
- javax
- junit
- org
- com
- kieker
- kieker.test

There must be a newline between imports of different groups. Inside a group the imports must be in alphabetical order. I know this is all a little bit picky, but it saves a lot of work down the road. issue.title: Project Module Dependencies Are not Correctly Used

repository.name: buildship
repository.description: The Eclipse Plug-ins for Gradle project.

issue.body:
When importing Kieker (https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker) on Fedora 38, eclipse keeps displaying compile errors. The project compiles fine with pure Gradle (e.g., `./gradlew assemble`). 

### Expected Behavior
I expect a multi module project to be importable and to recognize dependencies between modules. That means, if one `build.gradle` contains

```
dependencies {
	implementation project(':kieker-common')
```

the kieker-common project should be recognized as a dependency and it should be possible to use classes from this project.

### Current Behavior
The dependency is not fully recognized. The dependencies are marked as errorneous:
![grafik](https://github.com/eclipse/buildship/assets/4358467/a12f7def-e401-4369-bb6b-20c19db32f4c)
but at the same time, the build path seems to contain the project dependency:
![grafik](https://github.com/eclipse/buildship/assets/4358467/2351f7d9-580d-4b36-80c7-c91e6b672797)
Surprisingly, if I go to configuration and hit `F3`, the correct class is opened - so at some level, the dependency seems to be recognized.

Cleaning, refreshing, closing the project and opening it again, deleting `.metadata`, `~/.gradle` and `.settings` and importing again all did not solve the problem. Furthermore, this also occurs on a minimized version of the project, including only the two modules `kieker-common` and `kieker-monitoring`.

### Context
I am trying to run main classes in the Kieker project. This worked a few versions ago.

### Steps to Reproduce 

- Clone kieker: `git clone -b KIEKER-1966 https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker.git` 
- Import it: File -> Import -> Gradle -> Existing Gradle Project -> Next -> Choose root directory -> Next -> Next 
- Afterwards, the (very simple) project hierarchy should be displayed:
![grafik](https://github.com/eclipse/buildship/assets/4358467/e312a75b-7cf6-4005-8d62-957ec7b6b553)
- Click finish
- Open for example the `ConfigurationFactory` - the internal dependencies are missing


### Your Environment
Fedora 38,  eclipse Version: 2023-09 (4.29.0) Build id: 20230907-1323, buildship 3.1.7.v20230428-1350	

I've also tried 2022-03 and 2021-09, but both did not fix the problem.

issue.title: [KIEKER-1817] Kieker-AspectJ and OpenJDK 11

repository.name: kieker
repository.description: Kieker is an observability framework, that consists of an monitoring and tracing agent, and compatible analysis tools

issue.body:
JIRA Issue: https://kieker-monitoring.atlassian.net/browse/KIEKER-1817 Original Reporter: DaGeRe ***

Currently, I am trying to run Kieker using AspectJ instrumentation on OpenJDK 11. Unfortunately, every variant I try results in an error.

This error even occurs if I run the probe-aspectj example from kieker-examples: Running https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker-11-example (just the example with a container providing OpenJDK 11), an error like the attached error occurs. Unfortunately, I do not see where to further spot this error, which seems to be somehow related to the bytecode.

Is this a known issue with OpenJDK 11 / is there maybe a workaround to get AspectJ instrumentation running?

## Checklist: ## JIRA Comments: ### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Wed, 25 Mar 2020 16:25:55

Furthermore, running a simple hello world in maven with kieker-aspectj-instrumentation results in:

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: Update to static final field de.kiekertest2.Main.ajc$tjp_0 attempted from a different method (ajc$preClinit) than the initializer method <clinit>
at de.kiekertest2.Main.ajc$preClinit(Main.java:1)
at de.kiekertest2.Main.<clinit>(Main.java:1)

This can be reproduced in the kieker-11-example repo inside the container using

cd ../aspectj-maven/
mvn clean package
java -cp target/classes/ -javaagent:../kiekertest/lib/kieker-1.14-SNAPSHOT-aspectj.jar de.kiekertest2.Main
### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Wed, 25 Mar 2020 17:39:47

Building Kieker with Java 11 and recent gradle version requires some updates, e.g. dependencies for XML-Libraries. But even when building with Java 11 and updating AspectJ to 1.9.5 (https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/tree/java11 ), the same error occurs.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 2 Apr 2020 21:36:06

I can confirm this diagnosis. I'll try to assemble a minimal AspectJ setup without kieker to test whether this is an issue with AspectJ.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Fri, 3 Apr 2020 14:16:23

A key issue is that Kieker uses and links its aspectj javaagent with aspectj 1.8.2. That seems to be incompatible with Java 11. I've hacked the Kieker build of 1.14-RC in a way to use aspectj 1.9.5 and produced a kieker-1.14-aspectj.jar which works with your example when I use gradle 5.6 or 6.* (it seems to be not working with gradle 4.*)

However, to make this possible we would have to replace our gradle 4.* with gradle 6.* and this requires a ton of other changes which we cannot make in the release of 1.14. Honestly, my current hack skips all tests, as they have stopped working.

However, I can give you for now the working Java 11+aspectj 1.9.5 version of the agent. kieker-1.14-aspectj.jar

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 28 Apr 2020 10:51:56

We will have a new Kieker release in the coming weeks/days. There will be no fix in 1.14, but I will fix this issue in 1.15-SNAPSHOT right away, as our own jpetstore-6 will no longer work with Java 9+.

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 11 Jun 2020 19:15:01

Thanks for the fix, is it also available in some branch? I tried to redo it (https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker ), but it would be easier to reuse the same code. To make it usable with gradle 6, I also skipped tests and disabled findbugs (seems like an update to spotbugs would be necessary).

While the fix (both your jar and my source) works for the basic example, it does not work as soon as a final field is changed. To make this reproducible, I created a little example: https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker-11-example Currently, I do not see while this happens. Do you maybe have a hint where to further search for the reason?

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 11 Jun 2020 21:42:36

It is not yet in any branch, as it was just a short test to identify the key issues with this. To fix it in a stable fashion, we have to upgrade gradle first. And before we can upgrade gradle, we have to fix document generation in the current stack.
Therefore, we will fix this in the coming weeks. I would add this to this ticket as blocking, but jira is not really good in this discipline

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 11 Jun 2020 21:47:02

KIEKER-1806 Done must be fixed to be able to use newer aspectJ

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 12:20:32

Are there any news from your side on this issue?

Since your jar is not able to instrument final fields, I tried to build it on my own and to understand the AspectJ problem. In general, @Around advices on constructors setting final values do not work in Java 11 (or maybe 9+): https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64611859/is-it-possible-to-exclude-field-sets-in-aspectj/ (mwe https://github.com/DaGeRe/aspect-final-example ). As pointed out in the Stackoverflow answer, this is a general issue in AspectJ.

From my current point of view, there are two ways to fix this:

  1. Exclude Constructors from monitoring in general. This quick hack can be implemented quickly (e.g. https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/tree/java11_2 ) by change just the monitoredOperation pointcuts to @Pointcut("execution(* (..))") instead of @Pointcut("execution( *(..)) || execution(new(..))"). Then, constructors are also excluded from monitoring in Java 8, which is not very nice, but at least Monitoring is working in Java 11.
  2. Refactor the monitoring to use @Before and @After instead of @Around, at least for constructors. Therefore, it would be necessary to know the signature, start time etc. in the @After method, and saving them could be expensive.

Do you see another way of fixing/quick hacking this issue?

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 13:30:30

Yes. I am currently waiting for Thomas to say yes to my changes in KIEKER-1806 Done . If so the build has switched to a current gradle build which in turn allows to build with OpneJDK 11 which allows to use AspectJ.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 13:33:39

Sorry, I was the week of and it seems Github forgot to email me (strange). Thomas has already accepted my commit. I will look into the KIEKER-1806 Done fix.

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 14:57:49

Thanks for the update. Unfortunately, your branch does not build with Java 11 since XML libraries are missing. Additionally, I cannot execute probe-aspectj example since it contains an old wrapper, I also updated it and put both changes in a pull request (https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/pull/263 )

Nevertheless, I got some aspectj problems:

[AppClassLoader@3d4eac69] info successfully verified type kieker.monitoring.probe.aspectj.flow.operationExecution.FullInstrumentationNoGetterAndSetter exists. Originates from kieker/mo
nitoring/probe/aspectj/flow/operationExecution/FullInstrumentationNoGetterAndSetter.java
Fehler: Hauptklasse kieker.examples.monitoring.aspectj.BookstoreStarter kann nicht initialisiert werden
Ursache: java.lang.VerifyError: Expecting a stackmap frame at branch target 60
Exception Details:
Location:
kieker/examples/monitoring/aspectj/BookstoreStarter.main_aroundBody0([Ljava/lang/String;Lorg/aspectj/lang/JoinPoint;)V @32: if_icmpge
Reason:
Expected stackmap frame at this location.
Bytecode:
0000000: bb00 0259 b700 034d 2ab8 0004 3604 bb00
0000010: 0559 1504 b700 063a 0603 3608 1508 1504
0000020: a200 1cb2 0007 1508 ba00 0800 00b6 0009
0000030: 2c19 06b8 000a 8408 01a7 ffe3 1906 b600
0000040: 0bb1

Task :runMonitoring FAILED

FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.

When updating my branch, I had a similiar issue, but I currently do not see why this happens.

Also, if the Java update would succeed, the AspectJ-problem still would persist (since AspectJ, like in the so thread told, seems to have problems instrumenting classes with final variables). Do you see a solution for this?

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 15:58:56

By fully updating AspectJ (i.e. also including 1.9.6 in the aspectJJar), it was possible to get rid of the error message, but unfortunately, a new one appeared in aspectj-example:

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError
at kieker.monitoring.core.controller.MonitoringController.getInstance(MonitoringController.java:404)
at kieker.monitoring.probe.aspectj.flow.operationExecution.AbstractAspect.<clinit>(AbstractAspect.java:42)

Caused by: org.aspectj.lang.NoAspectBoundException: kieker.monitoring.probe.aspectj.flow.operationExecution.FullInstrumentationNoGetterAndSetter
at kieker.monitoring.probe.aspectj.flow.operationExecution.FullInstrumentationNoGetterAndSetter.aspectOf(FullInstrumentationNoGetterAndSetter.java:1)

Analyzing the aspect FullInstrumentationNoGetterAndSetter with javap -v seems fine (aspectOf is defined), so I currently do not see why this does not work. When building the branch https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/tree/java11_2, the .class-file is nearly equal. Do you maybe see why this does not work?

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Mon, 2 Nov 2020 15:41:44

Thank you for merging the branch!

After a hint in the stackoverflow question, it was possible for me to implement a workaround for the initializer-problem: https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/commit/1d634fff8ee624f507bb5dfad2e356390182695a#diff-a0c6754d860dd45b4136aab221966407eb12e58604bbdcdc877609ca2d7b1655I’ll test it deeper in the next days and keep you updated. If it fully works, using this branch (and only OperationExecutionAspectFull) would be a solution for me until a real fix is present.

To fix this in general, it would be possible to either wait until AspectJ comes up with an own solution (or to solve the issue inside of AspectJ), or to refactor all aspects into @Before and @After advices. I do not assume that refactoring of Before and After has a notable performance impact, but to be sure, it would be better to measure this.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 3 Nov 2020 11:20:32

We have once an discussion on a migration from around to before and after advices. The more modern Kieker probes based on IFlowRecord events could be ported easily. However, before starting with such changes, I would like to have a solid working testbed, i.e., Example in the Kieker code base. However, this might need an extensive discussion at a Kieker meeting.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 26 Jan 2021 00:43:52

How should we progress here?

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 26 Jan 2021 10:44:42

In my memory, we discussed at the last Kieker meeting that you would try to refactor the @Around aspect into @Before and @After aspects, which should solve the problem.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 26 Jan 2021 11:07:08

I would rather suggest to create separate new advice classes using the @Before and @After annotations and producing Before* and After* events which can be found in https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/tree/master/kieker-common/src-gen/kieker/common/record/flow/trace

However, you would need other analysis filter to generate OperationExecutionRecords from them.

This also depends on what you use to analyze your data, e.g., TeeTime-based Kieker filters/stages, old style Kieker pipe-and-filter API or something else.

Execute for every branch, create test reports and upload unit test

body:
One problem that arises on actions with PRs is that results can not be published since PR authors often do not have the rights to access the repository (https://github.com/actions/first-interaction/issues/10). While the tests run as usual, publishing the test results is not possible. 

From my point of view, the easiest solution would be to use two workflows:
- A workflow for regular runs which publish test results and
- A second workflow for PR-runs, which do not publish test results (and for them, you'd need to manually inspect the logs)

While this is not a very nice solution, I currently see no better option.

issue.title: [KIEKER-1817] Kieker-AspectJ and OpenJDK 11

repository.name: kieker
repository.description: Kieker is an observability framework, that consists of an monitoring and tracing agent, and compatible analysis tools

issue.body:
JIRA Issue: https://kieker-monitoring.atlassian.net/browse/KIEKER-1817 Original Reporter: DaGeRe ***

Currently, I am trying to run Kieker using AspectJ instrumentation on OpenJDK 11. Unfortunately, every variant I try results in an error.

This error even occurs if I run the probe-aspectj example from kieker-examples: Running https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker-11-example (just the example with a container providing OpenJDK 11), an error like the attached error occurs. Unfortunately, I do not see where to further spot this error, which seems to be somehow related to the bytecode.

Is this a known issue with OpenJDK 11 / is there maybe a workaround to get AspectJ instrumentation running?

## Checklist: ## JIRA Comments: ### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Wed, 25 Mar 2020 16:25:55

Furthermore, running a simple hello world in maven with kieker-aspectj-instrumentation results in:

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: Update to static final field de.kiekertest2.Main.ajc$tjp_0 attempted from a different method (ajc$preClinit) than the initializer method <clinit>
at de.kiekertest2.Main.ajc$preClinit(Main.java:1)
at de.kiekertest2.Main.<clinit>(Main.java:1)

This can be reproduced in the kieker-11-example repo inside the container using

cd ../aspectj-maven/
mvn clean package
java -cp target/classes/ -javaagent:../kiekertest/lib/kieker-1.14-SNAPSHOT-aspectj.jar de.kiekertest2.Main
### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Wed, 25 Mar 2020 17:39:47

Building Kieker with Java 11 and recent gradle version requires some updates, e.g. dependencies for XML-Libraries. But even when building with Java 11 and updating AspectJ to 1.9.5 (https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/tree/java11 ), the same error occurs.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 2 Apr 2020 21:36:06

I can confirm this diagnosis. I'll try to assemble a minimal AspectJ setup without kieker to test whether this is an issue with AspectJ.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Fri, 3 Apr 2020 14:16:23

A key issue is that Kieker uses and links its aspectj javaagent with aspectj 1.8.2. That seems to be incompatible with Java 11. I've hacked the Kieker build of 1.14-RC in a way to use aspectj 1.9.5 and produced a kieker-1.14-aspectj.jar which works with your example when I use gradle 5.6 or 6.* (it seems to be not working with gradle 4.*)

However, to make this possible we would have to replace our gradle 4.* with gradle 6.* and this requires a ton of other changes which we cannot make in the release of 1.14. Honestly, my current hack skips all tests, as they have stopped working.

However, I can give you for now the working Java 11+aspectj 1.9.5 version of the agent. kieker-1.14-aspectj.jar

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 28 Apr 2020 10:51:56

We will have a new Kieker release in the coming weeks/days. There will be no fix in 1.14, but I will fix this issue in 1.15-SNAPSHOT right away, as our own jpetstore-6 will no longer work with Java 9+.

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 11 Jun 2020 19:15:01

Thanks for the fix, is it also available in some branch? I tried to redo it (https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker ), but it would be easier to reuse the same code. To make it usable with gradle 6, I also skipped tests and disabled findbugs (seems like an update to spotbugs would be necessary).

While the fix (both your jar and my source) works for the basic example, it does not work as soon as a final field is changed. To make this reproducible, I created a little example: https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker-11-example Currently, I do not see while this happens. Do you maybe have a hint where to further search for the reason?

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 11 Jun 2020 21:42:36

It is not yet in any branch, as it was just a short test to identify the key issues with this. To fix it in a stable fashion, we have to upgrade gradle first. And before we can upgrade gradle, we have to fix document generation in the current stack.
Therefore, we will fix this in the coming weeks. I would add this to this ticket as blocking, but jira is not really good in this discipline

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Thu, 11 Jun 2020 21:47:02

KIEKER-1806 Done must be fixed to be able to use newer aspectJ

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 12:20:32

Are there any news from your side on this issue?

Since your jar is not able to instrument final fields, I tried to build it on my own and to understand the AspectJ problem. In general, @Around advices on constructors setting final values do not work in Java 11 (or maybe 9+): https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64611859/is-it-possible-to-exclude-field-sets-in-aspectj/ (mwe https://github.com/DaGeRe/aspect-final-example ). As pointed out in the Stackoverflow answer, this is a general issue in AspectJ.

From my current point of view, there are two ways to fix this:

  1. Exclude Constructors from monitoring in general. This quick hack can be implemented quickly (e.g. https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/tree/java11_2 ) by change just the monitoredOperation pointcuts to @Pointcut("execution(* (..))") instead of @Pointcut("execution( *(..)) || execution(new(..))"). Then, constructors are also excluded from monitoring in Java 8, which is not very nice, but at least Monitoring is working in Java 11.
  2. Refactor the monitoring to use @Before and @After instead of @Around, at least for constructors. Therefore, it would be necessary to know the signature, start time etc. in the @After method, and saving them could be expensive.

Do you see another way of fixing/quick hacking this issue?

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 13:30:30

Yes. I am currently waiting for Thomas to say yes to my changes in KIEKER-1806 Done . If so the build has switched to a current gradle build which in turn allows to build with OpneJDK 11 which allows to use AspectJ.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 13:33:39

Sorry, I was the week of and it seems Github forgot to email me (strange). Thomas has already accepted my commit. I will look into the KIEKER-1806 Done fix.

Additionally, I cannot execute probe-aspectj example since it contains an old wrapper, I also updated it and put both changes in a pull request (https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/pull/263 )

Nevertheless, I got some aspectj problems:

Also, if the Java update would succeed, the AspectJ-problem still would persist (since AspectJ, like in the so thread told, seems to have problems instrumenting classes with final variables). Do you see a solution for this?

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Sat, 31 Oct 2020 15:58:56

By fully updating AspectJ (i.e. also including 1.9.6 in the aspectJJar), it was possible to get rid of the error message, but unfortunately, a new one appeared in aspectj-example:

### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Mon, 2 Nov 2020 15:41:44

Thank you for merging the branch!

After a hint in the stackoverflow question, it was possible for me to implement a workaround for the initializer-problem: https://github.com/DaGeRe/kieker/commit/1d634fff8ee624f507bb5dfad2e356390182695a#diff-a0c6754d860dd45b4136aab221966407eb12e58604bbdcdc877609ca2d7b1655I’ll test it deeper in the next days and keep you updated. If it fully works, using this branch (and only OperationExecutionAspectFull) would be a solution for me until a real fix is present.

To fix this in general, it would be possible to either wait until AspectJ comes up with an own solution (or to solve the issue inside of AspectJ), or to refactor all aspects into @Before and @After advices. I do not assume that refactoring of Before and After has a notable performance impact, but to be sure, it would be better to measure this.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 3 Nov 2020 11:20:32

We have once an discussion on a migration from around to before and after advices. The more modern Kieker probes based on IFlowRecord events could be ported easily. ### 557058:62e50ed6-5f61-4540-a49c-a43b84d72ea5 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 26 Jan 2021 10:44:42

In my memory, we discussed at the last Kieker meeting that you would try to refactor the @Around aspect into @Before and @After aspects, which should solve the problem.

### 557058:b81a6b7f-b4c8-4105-83ac-47b039a57a19 (JIRA username) added a comment on Tue, 26 Jan 2021 11:07:08

I would rather suggest to create separate new advice classes using the @Before and @After annotations and producing Before* and After* events which can be found in https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/tree/master/kieker-common/src-gen/kieker/common/record/flow/trace

However, you would need other analysis filter to generate OperationExecutionRecords from them.

This also depends on what you use to analyze your data, e.g., TeeTime-based Kieker filters/stages, old style Kieker pipe-and-filter API or something else.

Is there a specific reason why the BinarySerializer tests are set to be ignored?

> Is there a specific reason why the BinarySerializer tests are set to be ignored?
> [aa3ce59](https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/commit/aa3ce59d1573c8c836106a85d4eb2aaac80b6840)
> [4af20c3](https://github.com/kieker-monitoring/kieker/commit/4af20c354cffafadff94f5112ae458d02dd83a75)
> As you mention "for now" in the commit message I was not sure whether this should be changed back before the merge.

Yes, I had the same question for the archives.

Both tests failed randomly. While working in the branch, they did not in the PR-251. I suspect that this is some sort of race condition, as no code changes where made anywhere. Changes in the build scripts only deactivated the tgz deliverables due to size restrictions (which we can take back when the archive gets smaller again due to an update in the build system). Thus, I temporarily deactivated the two tests to get the necessary Jenkinsfile changes into Kieker (which we need to be able to fix all the other related issues).

While deeper inspecting the test. It is highly suspicious. (a) it claims to test the BinarySerializer, but the serializer are in the project kieker-common. So wrong package. It is also not testing the BinarySerializer, but instead the use of it in context of the ChunkingCollector. However, I did not want to remove the code or just comment the test out (which would be also an option), but instead set two ignore tags which cause additional errors with Checkstyle forcing us to not forget the issue.

> Changes in the build scripts only deactivated the tgz deliverables due to size restrictions (which we can take back when the archive gets smaller again due to an update in the build system).

OK, I see. From your initial comment "production of zip and tgz result archives." I understood that you deactivated both ZIP and TGZ. In general, I think we could get rid of the TGZs.
Currently, we have severe disc space issues. Thus I cannot get anything built. Technicians willl fix this by end of the week.

body: What is the reason for putting test classes into a separate `test` package? As far as I know it is generally accepted good practice to put test classes in the the same package as the class under test, but (as we already do) in a separate directory structure. For example, to be able to test package-private classes or methods. Unfortunately no better sources than [[1]](https://softwareengineering.stackexchange.com/questions/328780/naming-convention-for-test-packages), [[2]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/811827/where-should-i-put-my-junit-tests), [[3]](http://www.kyleblaney.com/junit-best-practices/). I know, this is the convention in Kieker, but perhaps we should reconsider this practice.

body:
Either in addition or instead of the 'local-build.sh' script to execute the pipeline locally, we could also use a Docker-based solution to resemble the build as exact as possible (due to the unified environment with Docker).

Here is a draft for a Docker variant:

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash

####
# This script allows to run the all tasks in the same environment as it is
# executed on the Kieker build server.
#
# Example:
# ./runLocalPipeline.sh
# This would execute all tasks that are also executed in the Jenkins pipeline.
#
#
# Requirements:
# - Docker
###

# Check if user is in docker group
groups | grep docker >/dev/null

if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
  docker run -u `id -u` --rm -v `pwd`:/opt/kieker kieker/kieker-build:openjdk8 /bin/bash -c "\
    cd /opt/kieker;\
    ./gradlew clean && \
    ./gradlew compileJava compileTestJava &&\
    ./gradlew test &&\
    ./gradlew check &&\
    ./gradlew checkReleaseArchivesShort &&\
    ./gradlew checkReleaseArchives"
else
  echo "You are not in the docker group."
fi
```

body:
The PR failed once because of the timeout.
See: https://build.se.informatik.uni-kiel.de/jenkins/job/kieker-monitoring/job/kieker/view/change-requests/job/PR-151/1/console
Yes, sure. That's what the timeout is for ;) Currently, fetching from github is buggy. Even on my machine. So, it's not the fault of the timeout or of Jenkins.

The question I wanted to raise here is whether we want to fail the build in such cases. With the current setup (all) our builds would fail if there would be comparably small delay. This way we would have to re-issue the builds every time there is such a "buggy" condition.

I expected this timeout to be more aimed at the issue that we had 'hanging' builds that were locking up resources like our worker nodes. So the timeout would rather take care of terminating them after some time to free up the resources again.
So, do you propose to wrap the timeout around the whole pipeline? If not, I didn't get your point. The fetching would hang forever, if we do not interrupt it.

body: Please review and give me hints for wanted changes :-)

@aaschmid Thank you for your contribution! 
@ChristianWulf As far as I remember you were investigating these issues. Could you have a look please?

@aaschmid Thanks for your PR. However, the report file is generated with an invalid encoding name "Cp1252".
`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="Cp1252"?>
<pmd-cpd> ...`

Quoting from [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16141416/is-encoding-cp1252-invalid-in-an-xml-file):
> i guess the encoding you're looking for COULD be windows-1252. Cp1252 might be a valid charset in java, but in XML, you're not supposed to use it (by that name).

Could you please generate the file with a valid encoding name, preferably in UTF-8?

Hi @ChristianWulf,

You can simple add `encoding = 'UTF-8'` to the reports `xml` section. What is the real encoding of the file? Can you check with `file -i <filename>`?

Here is an example:

```
    reports {
        text.enabled = false
        xml {
            enabled = true
            encoding = 'UTF-8'
        }
```

But to be honest I am not sure if this is working properly in CPD itself. I am calling the XML renderer with the given encoding and my local tests generate the xml with that encoding in the encoding tag but the file seems to be still the platform encoding :-(

Cheers,
Andreas

Hi @aaschmid ,
works great! Thanks. Moreover, the output file's actual encoding is UTF-8.
